      endedMeasures: [],
      reviewed: {
        kind: corrected.kind,
        ground: corrected.ground,
        ruleId: corrected.ruleId,
        rulesVersion: corrected.rulesVersion,
        legalReference: corrected.legalReference,
        decidedAt: corrected.decidedAt,
        // 3e's review (people1): the basis of the corrected decision's suspension or termination, as the API's statement carries it.
        basis: corrected.actions.find((action) => action.kind === "suspend" || action.kind === "terminate")?.basis ?? null,
      },
      // Task 4: what an answer to the reply fixes, as far as the page can tell now.
      ...(draft.kind === "correction" ? { repliedTo: repliedToPreview(corrected, draft, now) } : {}),
    };
  }
  const restricts = draft.outcome === "restricted";
  const law = restricts && draft.ground === "illegal";
  const reach = view.suspicion?.reach ?? { posts: 0, images: 0 };
  // The facts and the reason are told with a decision that holds a measure. Those of a decision without one are the
  // case's record, for staff: the statement's data holds neither, here as in the API's own reading of the decision.
  const told = draft.actions.some((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts === null);
  return {
    ...base,
    kind: draft.kind,
    outcome: draft.outcome,
    ground: restricts ? draft.ground : null,
    ruleId: restricts && !law ? draft.ruleId : null,
    rulesVersion: RULES_VERSION,
    legalReference: law ? text("legal_reference") : null,
    facts: told ? text("facts") : null,
    reason: told ? text("reason") : null,
    source: predictedSource(view, draft.kind),
    measures: draft.actions
      .filter((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts === null)
      .map((action) => {
        const noEffect = noEffectOf(view, action, draft.kind === "final" ? "final" : "interim");
        // 3e Task 4: an announced suspension or termination, or a termination at once.
        if ((action.kind === "suspend" && action.announced === true) || action.kind === "terminate") return previewStanding(view, action, noEffect, now);
        // 3e Task 3: a suspension at once, with its basis, its end and the decision it rests on, as the database will fix them.
        if (action.kind === "suspend") return previewSuspension(view, draft, action, noEffect, now);
        // 3e Task 5: a warning about reporting or a restriction of it, with its end and the warning a restriction follows.
        if (action.kind === "warn_reporting" || action.kind === "restrict_reporting") return previewReporting(view, action, noEffect, now);
        const measure = { kind: action.kind as MeasureKind, mediaId: action.mediaId, noEffect, sealed: action.kind === "seal_media" ? { posts: reach.posts, images: reach.images, deletedImages: 0 } : null };
        // 3e: a retirement names the snapshot's handle, and the placeholder's form when it changes the profile.
        if (action.kind !== "retire_handle") return measure;
        return { ...measure, handle: snapshotHandle(view) ?? (view.target.type === "account" ? (view.target.handle?.toLowerCase() ?? null) : null), placeholder: noEffect === null ? PREVIEW_PLACEHOLDER : null };
      })
      // 3e: the strike the params will carry, until when it counts (decided now) and the strikes that count with it.
      .concat(
        strikeOf(view, draft).map(() => ({
          kind: "strike" as MeasureKind,
          mediaId: null,
          noEffect: null,
          sealed: null,
          endsAt: new Date(now.getTime() + STANDING_RULES.strikeDays * DAY_MS).toISOString(),
          activeThen: ACTIVE_THEN[view.authorStanding?.activeStrikes ?? "0"],
        })),
      ),
    reversals: draft.actions.filter((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts !== null).map((action) => ({ kind: action.kind as ReversalKind, mediaId: action.mediaId, ...NO_RESET })),
    endedMeasures: endedBy(view, draft),
    reviewed: null,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the params and the confirmation

/** The digest of a snapshot, computed here from the members the page displayed: never the digest the answer carried. */
export function shownSnapshotDigest(snapshot: Extract<CaseSnapshot, { withheld: false }>): Promise<string> {
  return snapshotDigest({
    salt: snapshot.salt,
    targetType: snapshot.targetType,
    targetId: snapshot.targetId,
    takenAt: snapshot.takenAt,
    authorHandle: snapshot.authorHandle,
    postState: snapshot.postState,
    postCreatedAt: snapshot.postCreatedAt,
    replyToId: snapshot.replyToId,
    quoteOfId: snapshot.quoteOfId,
    body: snapshot.body,
    media: snapshot.media,
    displayName: snapshot.displayName,
    bio: snapshot.bio,
    handle: snapshot.handle,
  });
}

/** The digests a decision's params carry: the shown snapshot's, and those of the texts the console saved. */
export interface DecisionDigests {
  snapshot: string;
  facts: string | null;
  reason: string | null;
  legalReference: string | null;
}

/**
 * The params the key confirms, built from what the page shows (3c design, section 7.5, step 1): the case's version, the
 * range a final decision answers, the newest snapshot by its id with the digest the console computed, the digests of the
 * saved texts and the actions in their one order. The contracts' schema refuses what cannot stand before any key is asked.
 */
export function decisionParamsOf(view: CaseView, draft: CaseDraft, digests: DecisionDigests): CaseDecidedParams {
  const newest = view.snapshots[0];
  if (!newest) throw new Error("a decision names a snapshot of its case: the case holds none");
  const corrected = draft.kind === "correction" ? view.decisions.find((decided) => decided.id === draft.reviewsDecisionId) : undefined;
  if (draft.kind === "correction" && !corrected) throw new Error("a correction's draft names a decision of the case");
  // 3e: the strike the case answer says is due, and the overruling of a full correction, are the console's to add: the
  // person never chooses either. A kept answer to a reply, and a kept correction that withdraws a decision's marks, lift
  // nothing and overrule nothing. Task 5: a final "No breach" decision signs the marks its person ticked on the items it
  // answers; any other signs none, and a withdrawal of marks signs no list either (the database withdraws them all).
  const kept = draft.answer === "kept" || draft.withdrawMarks === true;
  const added = draft.kind === "correction" ? (kept ? [] : overruleOf(corrected, reversesAll(view, draft))) : strikeOf(view, draft);
  const actions = [...draft.actions, ...added].sort(compareDecisionActions);
  const unfounded = draft.kind === "correction" ? [] : marksOf(view, draft);
  const shared = { stateVersion: view.stateVersion, snapshotId: newest.id, snapshotDigest: digests.snapshot, redressVersion: REDRESS_VERSION, actions, unfounded, replaced: draft.kind === "correction" && draft.replaced === true };
  if (draft.kind === "correction" && corrected) {
    return CaseDecidedParams.parse({
      ...shared,
      kind: "correction",
      throughSeq: 0,
      reviewsDecisionId: corrected.id,
      outcome: kept ? "kept" : reversesAll(view, draft) ? "reversed" : "partly_reversed",
      ground: null,
      ruleId: null,
      // A correction carries the rulebook version and the category of the decision it corrects.
      rulesVersion: corrected.rulesVersion,
      category: corrected.category,
      categoryKeyword: null,
      factsDigest: null,
      reasonDigest: digests.reason,
      legalReferenceDigest: null,
    });
  }
  const restricts = draft.outcome === "restricted";
  const law = restricts && draft.ground === "illegal";
  return CaseDecidedParams.parse({
    ...shared,
    kind: draft.kind,
    throughSeq: draft.kind === "final" ? throughSeqOf(view) : 0,
    reviewsDecisionId: null,
    outcome: draft.outcome,
    ground: restricts ? draft.ground : null,
    ruleId: restricts && !law ? draft.ruleId : null,
    rulesVersion: RULES_VERSION,
    category: draft.category,
    categoryKeyword: law && draft.terrorist ? "KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT" : null,
    // A restriction carries both; a decision without a measure carries each when it was written.
    factsDigest: digests.facts,
    reasonDigest: digests.reason,
    legalReferenceDigest: law ? digests.legalReference : null,
  });
}

/** The texts whose fields a draft's decision has on the page, in the order they are saved. */
export function textsOffered(draft: CaseDraft): DraftTextKind[] {
  if (draft.kind === "correction" || draft.kind === "review") return ["review_reason"];
  return draft.outcome === "restricted" && draft.ground === "illegal" ? ["facts", "reason", "legal_reference"] : ["facts", "reason"];
}

/**
 * The texts a draft's decision cannot do without. A restriction needs its facts and its reason, and on the law its legal
 * reference; a correction its reason. A decision without a measure may leave both of its texts empty, except an answer to
 * a report or finding of child sexual abuse material: an admin decides it without seeing the images, and says in the
 * facts what the answer rested on.
 */
export function textsRequired(view: CaseView, draft: CaseDraft): DraftTextKind[] {
  if (draft.kind === "correction" || draft.kind === "review" || draft.outcome === "restricted") return textsOffered(draft);
  return suspectOpen(view).length > 0 ? ["facts"] : [];
}

/** Whether a draft holds what its decision needs before anything is sent: something to do, and each text it cannot do without. */
export function complete(view: CaseView, draft: CaseDraft): boolean {
  if (textsRequired(view, draft).some((kind) => normalised(draft.written[kind]) === "")) return false;
  // 3e: a kept answer to a reply lifts nothing; every other correction lifts something.
  if (draft.kind === "correction") return draft.answer === "kept" ? draft.actions.length === 0 : draft.actions.length > 0;
  if (draft.kind === "review") return reviewConsistent(view, draft);
  return draft.outcome !== "restricted" || draft.actions.some((action) => MEASURES[action.kind].lifts === null);
}

/** What saving one text of a draft came to: the saved text, the console's words for a refusal with its code, or null when there was nothing to save. */
export type TextSaveOutcome = { saved: SavedText } | { error: string; code: string } | null;

/**
 * Saves one text of a draft, without the key (3c design, section 7.4): when its field loses focus, and again at Confirm
 * for a text that is not saved yet. Nothing is sent for an empty text, or for one whose normalised form is the one saved
 * already. A refusal comes back in the console's words; nothing is thrown, and the draft is not touched: what was
 * written stays with the caller, which saves it again at the next occasion.
 */
export async function saveDraftText(deps: { api: StaffApi; random?: RandomBytes }, caseId: CaseId, draft: CaseDraft, kind: DraftTextKind): Promise<TextSaveOutcome> {
  const text = normalised(draft.written[kind]);
  if (text === "" || draft.texts[kind]?.text === text) return null;
  try {
    const saved = await saveStaffText(deps, caseId, kind, draft.written[kind]);
    return { saved: { id: saved.id, text: saved.text, salt: saved.salt, digest: saved.digest } };
  } catch (err) {
    return { error: describeError(err, NOTE_WORDS), code: codeOf(err) ?? "internal" };
  }
}

/** The codes after which the case, or its snapshot, is no longer what the page shows: the refusal's words say to read or to take a snapshot again. */
const STALE_CODES: readonly string[] = ["case_changed", "profile_changed", "snapshot_erased", "snapshot_mismatch"];

/**
 * What the page does about a refused confirmation, beside wording it in place with the draft kept: it reads the case
 * again when the refusal says that the case or its snapshot changed, so that "take a fresh snapshot and decide again" can
 * be followed on the spot; and it forgets which texts it saved when one of them is gone or was used, so that the next
 * Confirm saves them again.
 */
export function afterRefusal(code: string): { readAgain: boolean; saveAgain: boolean } {
  return { readAgain: STALE_CODES.includes(code), saveAgain: code === "text_not_found" };
}

/**
 * The page's words after a decision was recorded: on a final decision, which reports the range left open for later, and
 * how many items arrived since the page read the case, which stay open too.
 */
export function decidedNotice(before: CaseView, now: CaseView, wasFinal: boolean): string {
  const words: string[] = [COMPOSER.recorded];
  if (!wasFinal) return words.join(" ");
  const left = leftOpen(before).length;
  const open = now.items.filter((item) => item.outcome === null).length;
  if (left > 0) words.push(COMPOSER.leftForLater(left));
  if (open > left) words.push(COMPOSER.arrivedSince(open - left));
  // The page showed a decision that closes the case and ends what was done while deciding; an item that arrived meanwhile
  // kept the case open, and with it those measures.
  const staying = left === 0 && open > 0 && now.closedAt === null ? interimInForce(now).map(({ action }) => MEASURES[action.kind].label) : [];
  if (staying.length > 0) words.push(COMPOSER.interimStays(staying.join(", ")));
  return words.join(" ");
}

/** What a confirmation needs of the page that runs it: whether it is still open, what it shows and holds now, the saves of texts on their way, and its busy flag. */
export interface ConfirmingPage {
  alive(): boolean;
  /** The case the page shows, or null when it shows none (a read failed for good). */
  shown(): CaseView | null;
  draft(): CaseDraft | null;
  saving(): readonly Promise<unknown>[];
  setBusy(busy: boolean): void;
}

/**
 * One confirmation with the page's busy flag around it. The flag goes up before anything is awaited and comes down on
 * every way out while the page is still open: when `run` has ended, when it threw, and when the page shows no case or
 * holds no draft any more after the wait, so that the composer is never left switched off. The click that confirms also
 * takes the focus from a text's field: that save ends first, so that its text is not saved twice, and `run` gets the
 * case and the draft as they stand after it.
 */
export async function confirmWhileBusy(page: ConfirmingPage, run: (view: CaseView, draft: CaseDraft) => Promise<void>): Promise<void> {
  if (page.shown() === null || page.draft() === null) return;
  page.setBusy(true);
  try {
    await Promise.allSettled(page.saving());
    const [view, draft] = [page.shown(), page.draft()];
    if (!page.alive() || view === null || draft === null) return;
    await run(view, draft);
  } finally {
    if (page.alive()) page.setBusy(false);
  }
}

/**
 * What "Confirm with your staff key" comes to: the case as it now stands; or a fresh snapshot that the page must show
 * before anything is confirmed; or the console's words for the step that failed, with its code, the draft kept.
 */
export type ConfirmOutcome = { view: CaseView } | { fresh: CaseView; notice: string } | { error: string; code: string };

/**
 * The decision as the page runs it (3c design, section 7.5, step 1). `caseId` is the case of the page's address: the
 * texts are saved on it and the key confirms a decision on it, never on whatever case an answer named. In this order:
 *   1. a view of another case than the page's, or a draft that lacks a measure or a text it needs, is not sent at all;
 *   2. when the case's newest snapshot cannot be shown (withheld, erased, or none), a fresh one is taken and the case
 *      read again, and nothing is confirmed: the page shows it first, so no decision names a snapshot nobody was shown;
 *   3. each text that is written is saved, without the key, unless the same text was saved before (when its field lost
 *      focus, or at an earlier try); the digest is the one computed here (saveStaffText refuses an answer that carries
 *      another), and `remember` is told of each save;
 *   4. the snapshot's digest is computed from what the page displayed;
 *   5. the params are built and checked, and the key confirms exactly them; the answer is the case as it now stands. A
 *      review is confirmed as its own action, on the decision whose appeal it answers.
 * Nothing is thrown: a refusal comes back as the console's words for its code.
 */
export async function confirmDecision(
  deps: { api: StaffApi; credentials: CredentialsLike; random?: RandomBytes },
  caseId: CaseId,
  view: CaseView,
  draft: CaseDraft,
  remember: (kind: DraftTextKind, saved: SavedText) => void = () => undefined,
): Promise<ConfirmOutcome> {
  const refusal = (err: unknown): ConfirmOutcome => ({ error: describeError(err), code: codeOf(err) ?? "internal" });
  if (view.id !== caseId) return { error: messageFor("invalid_answer"), code: "invalid_answer" };
  if (!complete(view, draft)) return { error: COMPOSER.incomplete, code: "incomplete" };

  const newest = view.snapshots[0];
  if (!newest || newest.withheld) {
    try {
      await deps.api.takeSnapshot(caseId, { activity: true });
      return { fresh: await deps.api.caseView(caseId, { activity: true }), notice: COMPOSER.freshSnapshot };
    } catch (err) {
      return refusal(err);
    }
  }

  const digests: Partial<Record<DraftTextKind, string>> = {};
  for (const kind of textsOffered(draft)) {
    const outcome = await saveDraftText(deps, caseId, draft, kind);
    if (outcome !== null && "error" in outcome) return outcome;
    if (outcome !== null) remember(kind, outcome.saved);
    // Saved just now, saved before, or left empty: an empty text has no digest.
    const digest = outcome?.saved.digest ?? (normalised(draft.written[kind]) === "" ? undefined : draft.texts[kind]?.digest);
    if (digest !== undefined) digests[kind] = digest;
  }

  if (draft.kind === "review") {
    // A review is confirmed as the action of its own: on the decision it reviews, with its appeal among the params.
    let reviewed: AppealsReviewedParams;
    try {
      reviewed = reviewParamsOf(view, draft, { snapshot: await shownSnapshotDigest(newest), reason: digests.review_reason ?? null });
    } catch {
      return { error: COMPOSER.incomplete, code: "incomplete" };
    }
    try {
      return { view: await reviewWithKey(deps, caseId, draft.reviewsDecisionId ?? "", reviewed) };
    } catch (err) {
      return refusal(err);
    }
  }

  let params: CaseDecidedParams;
  try {
    params = decisionParamsOf(view, draft, {
      snapshot: await shownSnapshotDigest(newest),
      facts: digests.facts ?? null,
      reason: draft.kind === "correction" ? (digests.review_reason ?? null) : (digests.reason ?? null),
      legalReference: digests.legal_reference ?? null,
    });
  } catch {
    return { error: COMPOSER.incomplete, code: "incomplete" };
  }
  try {
    return { view: await decideWithKey(deps, caseId, params) };
  } catch (err) {
    return refusal(err);
  }
}

import { REPLY_AIM_HOURS, RETENTION, STANDING_RULES, type AppealsReviewedParams, type AuthorStanding, type CaseDecision, type ItemOutcome, type ModerationErrorCode, type ReviewerState, type StaffErrorCode } from "@korbat/contracts";

/**
 * The console's own words for every code it can receive (3a design, section 10) and for every outcome it shows (3c
 * design, section 8), one table each. The server's message is never shown: the console words each code from these
 * tables, so a changed or hostile API answer cannot put its own text on the page, and no staff screen ever shows the
 * text of a passkey code, whose remedies are the app's.
 */

/** The ten staff codes, in the design's words. */
export const STAFF_MESSAGES: Record<StaffErrorCode, string> = {
  staff_session_required: "Your staff session ended. Sign in with your staff key.",
  staff_key_invalid: "This key does not open the staff console. If it should, ask the operator to check your staff keys.",
  staff_key_suspended: "This staff key was switched off because a copy of it may exist. Ask the operator for a link to enrol a new one.",
  staff_key_limit: "This account has 5 staff keys. Ask the operator to revoke one before enrolling another.",
  staff_key_not_device_bound: "This key can be synced or copied, so it cannot be a staff key. Use a security key or a device-bound authenticator.",
  staff_key_not_user_verified: "This key did not ask for a PIN or fingerprint, so it cannot be a staff key. Set a PIN on it, or use another key.",
  staff_key_refused: "The browser's answer for this key could not be checked. Try again, or use another key; this link still works.",
  staff_enrollment_invalid: "This enrolment link has expired or was already used. Ask the operator for a new one.",
  staff_step_up_required: "Confirm this with your staff key.",
  staff_step_up_invalid: "That confirmation was for another action, was already used or could not be checked. Try again.",
};

/**
 * 3e (design, section 8.3): the two sentences that also word a code of the moderation table, the standing measure that
 * is already in the way and a termination under R2.
 */
const STANDING_CONFLICT =
  'Not open: a suspension or termination of this account already stands and has not ended. To change it, lift it first with a correction of its decision. If it is announced and has not started, and an admin must take a measure at once, use "Withdraw it for another measure" on that decision: the person is then told that korbat withdrew it for another measure, not that their reply succeeded.';
const STANDING_TERMINATE_R2 =
  "No termination under R2: korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them and nothing is established. A protective suspension is the most a sealed report allows.";

/**
 * The console's sentences about an account's standing (3e design, section 8), each under the design's key. Every number
 * in one is printed from STANDING_RULES or from the answer, never typed, so that a table test can hold them.
 */

      law: "No strike: a decision on the law alone never gives one.",

      already: "No strike: this post already carries a strike that stands.",
      before: "No strike: the author posted this before they were told of their newest strike, so it is no repeat after that warning.",

/**
 * The moderation codes the console can meet (3c design, sections 8 and 10): those of the case routes, of a decision, of
 * a review, of a finding's link and of a reveal. The codes of the app's own report form, appeal and re-examination never
 * reach the console.
 */
export const CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES = [
  "notice_link_invalid",
  "notice_link_offsite",
  "case_changed",
  "case_closed",
  "staff_recused",
  "staff_target",
  "admin_required",
  "reviewer_conflict",
  "decision_cap",
  "profile_changed",
  "snapshot_mismatch",
  "snapshot_erased",
  "text_invalid",
  "text_quotes_user",
  "text_not_found",
  "invalid_decision",
  "image_refused",
  "reveal_refused",
  // 3e (design, section 8.9): the first three are the ones the composer meets; the other two cannot reach the console
  // today and are worded so that the table has an entry for each code of the type.
  "strike_mismatch",
  "standing_conflict",
  "ground_not_established",
  "reply_not_open",
  "reporting_restricted",
] as const satisfies readonly ModerationErrorCode[];
export type ConsoleModerationCode = (typeof CONSOLE_MODERATION_CODES)[number];

/** The console's words for each of them. A recusal reads the same whether the conflict concerns the author or a reporter. */
export const MODERATION_MESSAGES: Record<ConsoleModerationCode, string> = {
  notice_link_invalid: "That link does not name a post or a profile on korbat.",
  notice_link_offsite: "That link leads to another site. A case is opened only on a post or a profile of this korbat.",
  case_changed: "The case changed since this page read it. Read it again, check it and decide again.",
  case_closed: "The case changed at that moment. Try again.",
  staff_recused:
    "You cannot open or decide this case: an account linked to you takes part in it, or follows, blocks, mutes or replied to someone who does, or the post replies to or quotes a post of an account linked to you. Another staff member must handle it.",
  staff_target: "A final decision cannot restrict a staff account: staff are disciplined by demotion. A measure taken while deciding can.",
  admin_required: "Only an admin can take this decision.",
  reviewer_conflict: "You cannot review this appeal: you made a decision in its case, or opened a finding in it. Another staff member must review it.",
  decision_cap: "You have reached the limit on decisions one staff account may confirm for now. Try again later.",

  toAuthor: "The author receives this text by email and keeps it while their account exists.",

  previewAfterSnapshot: "The preview follows the fresh snapshot: the case's newest snapshot cannot be shown, so Confirm takes a fresh one, shows it, and asks you to confirm again.",
  sealSettled: "The numbers, the sentence about posts their author had deleted, and whether the seal changes anything are settled when the seal is recorded: the statement its author gets holds them as they are then.",
} as const;

/**
 * The shared codes a staff route may also answer, and the console's own: a network failure, an answer its schemas refuse,
 * a browser prompt that did not finish, step-up options that bind something other than the action the person chose, and
 * sign-in or enrolment options whose challenge is not one of that ceremony's.
 */
const OTHER_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  challenge_expired: "That took too long. Try again.",
  rate_limited: "Too many attempts. Wait a while, then try again.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  not_found: "That no longer exists.",
  csrf_failed: "This request could not be verified. Reload the page and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
  internal: "Something went wrong on the server. Try again.",
  network: "The staff console's server cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.",
  invalid_answer: "The server's answer could not be read. Reload the page and try again.",
  ceremony_cancelled: "Nothing was signed: the browser's prompt was closed or timed out. Try again.",
  key_already_registered: "This key is already registered for your staff account. Use another key.",
  ceremony_refused: "The browser refused to use a key here. Open the console at exactly the address in CONSOLE_ORIGIN, never at 127.0.0.1, and try again.",
  step_up_mismatch:
    "The confirmation could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than this action, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  signin_mismatch:
    "The sign-in could not be checked: the server asked your key to sign something other than a sign-in, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
  enroll_mismatch:
    "The registration could not be checked: the server asked your key for something other than a staff key's registration, so your key was not asked. Reload the page and try again; if it happens again, tell the operator.",
};

const FALLBACK = "Something went wrong. Try again.";

/** The console's words for a code; a code it does not know, a passkey code included, gets the plain fallback. */
export function messageFor(code: string): string {
  if (Object.hasOwn(STAFF_MESSAGES, code)) return STAFF_MESSAGES[code as StaffErrorCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(MODERATION_MESSAGES, code)) return MODERATION_MESSAGES[code as ConsoleModerationCode];
  if (Object.hasOwn(OTHER_MESSAGES, code)) return OTHER_MESSAGES[code]!;
  return FALLBACK;
}

/** The code of anything a screen's action threw, or null: the console's errors carry one. */
export function codeOf(err: unknown): string | null {
  return err instanceof Error && "code" in err && typeof err.code === "string" ? err.code : null;
}

/**
 * The words for anything a screen's action threw: the console's errors carry a code, anything else is the fallback.
 * `words` gives a screen's own words for a code where the shared ones would say too little: which daily limit was
 * reached, or what a link that names nothing means on the form it was typed into.
 */
export function describeError(err: unknown, words: Record<string, string> = {}): string {
  const code = codeOf(err);
  if (code === null) return FALLBACK;
  return Object.hasOwn(words, code) ? words[code]! : messageFor(code);
}

import { FINDING_CATEGORIES, FindingRequest, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY, RULE_IDS, type QueueReply, type QueueRow, type RuleId, type TdbCategory } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { getRule } from "@korbat/rules";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState, type FormEvent } from "react";
import type { StaffApi } from "../api";
import { systemClock, type Clock } from "../idle";
import { describeError, FINDING_WORDS, STANDING_WORDS } from "../messages";

import { parseCaseId, type CaseId } from "../router";
import { dateTime, Loaded, type Loadable } from "../ui";
import { categoryLabel, counted, LANE_NAMES, waited } from "../words";

/**
 * The queue (3c design, sections 7.3 and 8): open cases by lane and then by age, as the API orders them. Nothing here
 * weighs a case: no count of reports, no standing of a reporter. The page reads the queue again every 60 seconds without
 * the activity mark, so a queue left open never keeps a staff session alive. Beside it, "Open a case" takes a korbat link
 * on the moderator's own finding.
 */

/** How often the queue reads itself again. */
export const QUEUE_REFRESH_MS = 60_000;

/**
 * The screen's reads of the queue, on a clock that is the page's or a test's (as the idle timer's is): one now, marked,
 * since opening the screen is its person's action, and one every QUEUE_REFRESH_MS after it, unmarked, since those are the
 * page's own and must never move the session's idle end. Answers what ends them, for when the screen is left.
 */
export function startQueueReads(clock: Clock, read: (activity: boolean) => void): () => void {
  let handle: unknown = null;
  let ended = false;
  const refresh = () => {
    if (ended) return;
    read(false);
    handle = clock.setTimeout(refresh, QUEUE_REFRESH_MS);
  };
  read(true);
  handle = clock.setTimeout(refresh, QUEUE_REFRESH_MS);
  return () => {
    ended = true;
    clock.clearTimeout(handle);
  };
}

/** What marks a row beyond its lane and age: the console's own words for what its unanswered items are. */
export function marksOf(row: QueueRow): string[] {
  const marks: string[] = [];
  if (row.allegesIllegal) marks.push("notice under Art. 16");
  if (row.suspect) marks.push("CSAM: no images");
  if (row.reexamination) marks.push("re-examination");
  if (row.deferred) marks.push("deferred");
  return marks;
}

export interface FindingFormState {

export interface QueueViewProps {

  replies?: QueueReply[];
  /** Whether the API named a further page. */
  more: boolean;
  loadingMore: boolean;
  /** The time the ages are counted to. */
  now: number;
  finding: FindingFormState;
  onLoadMore(): void;
  onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void;
  onFindingChange(change: Partial<Pick<FindingFormState, "link" | "ruleId" | "category">>): void;
  onFindingSubmit(): void;
}

/**
 * 3e Task 4 (design, section 8.5): one reply in "Replies to answer": how long it has waited; before the start (the
 * suspension is held) or after it, until or since its end; the measure; and whether it has waited longer than korbat's
 * aim. The reply's text is read on the case page, where the access log and the recusal apply.
 */
export function replyWords(reply: QueueReply, now: number): string[] {
  const where = reply.onTime
    ? STANDING_WORDS.reply.before
    : reply.endsAt !== null && Date.parse(reply.endsAt) <= now
      ? STANDING_WORDS.reply.afterEnded(dateTime(reply.endsAt))
      : // A termination has no end: its row names none (3e's review, people9).
        reply.kind === "terminate" || reply.endsAt === null
        ? STANDING_WORDS.reply.afterTermination
        : STANDING_WORDS.reply.after(dateTime(reply.endsAt));
  const what = reply.kind === "terminate" ? STANDING_WORDS.reply.termination : STANDING_WORDS.reply.suspension(reply.days ?? 1);
  const late = now - Date.parse(reply.filedAt) > REPLY_AIM_HOURS * 60 * 60 * 1000 ? [STANDING_WORDS.reply.overAim] : [];
  return [where, what, ...late];
}

function Replies({ replies, now, onOpenCase }: { replies: QueueReply[]; now: number; onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void }) {

/** The finding a form's values make, or null when the link is no web address of at most 300 characters: the contracts' schema decides. */
export function findingOf(form: Pick<FindingFormState, "link" | "ruleId" | "category">): FindingRequest | null {
  const parsed = FindingRequest.safeParse({ target: { kind: "link", url: form.link.trim() }, ground: "rule", ruleId: form.ruleId, category: form.category });
  return parsed.success ? parsed.data : null;
}

/**
 * Reads the queue from its start through as many pages as the screen shows, one after the other. `activity` says whether
 * a person's action started the read: the screen's opening and "Load more" do, its own refresh every minute does not.
 */
export async function readQueue(api: StaffApi, pages: number, activity: boolean): Promise<{ rows: QueueRow[]; next: string | null; replies: QueueReply[] }> {
  const rows: QueueRow[] = [];
  const replies: QueueReply[] = [];
  let cursor: string | null = null;
  for (let page = 0; page < Math.max(1, pages); page++) {
    const answer = await api.queue(cursor, { activity });
    rows.push(...answer.cases);
    // Only the first page carries the replies.
    replies.push(...answer.replies);
    cursor = answer.nextCursor;
    if (cursor === null) break;
  }
  return { rows, next: cursor, replies };
}

export function Queue({ api, onOpenCase, clock = systemClock }: { api: StaffApi; onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void; clock?: Clock }) {
  const [rows, setRows] = useState<Loadable<QueueRow[]>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [replies, setReplies] = useState<QueueReply[]>([]);
  const [next, setNext] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [pages, setPages] = useState(1);
  const [loadingMore, setLoadingMore] = useState(false);
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  const [finding, setFinding] = useState<FindingFormState>({ link: "", ruleId: "R1", category: RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY.R1, busy: false, error: null });
  const alive = useRef(true);
  const shown = useRef(1);

  useEffect(() => {
    alive.current = true;
    const read = (activity: boolean) =>
      readQueue(api, shown.current, activity).then(
        (answer) => {
          if (!alive.current) return;
          setRows({ state: "ready", value: answer.rows });
          setReplies(answer.replies);
          setNext(answer.next);
          setNow(Date.now());
        },
        // A refresh that fails leaves the list as it was; only the first read shows its failure.
        (err: unknown) => alive.current && activity && setRows({ state: "failed", message: describeError(err) }),
      );
    const stop = startQueueReads(clock, (activity) => void read(activity));
    return () => {
      alive.current = false;
      stop();
    };
    // Read from the opening of the screen on; neither the API client nor the clock changes while the page lives.
  }, [api, clock]);

  const loadMore = async () => {
    if (next === null || rows.state !== "ready") return;
    setLoadingMore(true);
    try {
      const answer = await api.queue(next, { activity: true });
      if (!alive.current) return;
      shown.current = pages + 1;
      setPages(pages + 1);
      setRows({ state: "ready", value: [...rows.value, ...answer.cases] });
      setNext(answer.nextCursor);
    } catch (err) {
      if (alive.current) setRows({ state: "failed", message: describeError(err) });
    } finally {
      if (alive.current) setLoadingMore(false);
    }
  };

  const openFinding = async () => {
    const request = findingOf(finding);
    if (request === null) {
      setFinding((form) => ({ ...form, error: FINDING_WORDS.invalid_request }));
      return;
    }
    setFinding((form) => ({ ...form, busy: true, error: null }));
    try {
      const answer = await api.openFinding(request, { activity: true });
      const id = parseCaseId(answer.caseId);
      if (!alive.current) return;
      setFinding((form) => ({ ...form, busy: false, link: "" }));
      if (id) onOpenCase(id);
    } catch (err) {
      if (alive.current) setFinding((form) => ({ ...form, busy: false, error: describeError(err, FINDING_WORDS) }));
    }
  };

  return (
    <QueueView
      rows={rows}
      replies={replies}
      more={next !== null}
      loadingMore={loadingMore}
      now={now}
      finding={finding}
      onLoadMore={() => void loadMore()}
      onOpenCase={onOpenCase}
      // Choosing a rule presets its category; the moderator may still choose another.
      onFindingChange={(change) => setFinding((form) => ({ ...form, ...change, ...(change.ruleId ? { category: RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY[change.ruleId] } : {}), error: null }))}
      onFindingSubmit={() => void openFinding()}
    />
  );
}

export const BADGE_STARTS_PER_HOUR = 3;
/** Per client address, as the sign-up starts limit theirs: one address cannot run many accounts' starts. */
export const BADGE_STARTS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR = 10;
/** On the whole instance: every start is a text the provider bills, so no crowd of fresh accounts can run up the bill. */
export const BADGE_STARTS_PER_DAY = 200;

/** A flow id is a bearer credential while its verification is pending, so the store holds only its hash. */
export const badgeKey = (flowId: string) => `badge:${sha256Hex(flowId)}`;
/** The flow's attempts, counted by the store's atomic counter under the hashed flow id. */
export const badgeAttemptsKey = (flowId: string) => `badge-attempts:${sha256Hex(flowId)}`;

/**
 * The verification a code is out for, kept under the hashed flow id until the code is right or the ten
 * minutes pass. It holds the number only as its keyed hash, which is what the account will store; the
 * number itself went to the provider and nowhere else. The expiry is kept so that a state the store has
 * not dropped yet at the end of its ten minutes is still treated as gone. It is written once and never
 * written back: attempts are counted apart, atomically.
 */
export interface PendingBadge {
  userId: string;
  phoneHash: string;
  reference: string;
  expiresAt: number;
}

/**
 * The configured provider, or badge_unavailable (404) when VERIFY_PROVIDER is off. The web app does not
 * learn this from the answer: its build flag (EXPO_PUBLIC_BADGE, from WEB_BADGE) decides whether the badge
 * section is shown, off by default like the provider.
 */
function provider(deps: AuthDeps): VerificationProvider {
  if (!deps.verify) throw new AuthError("badge_unavailable", 404);
  return deps.verify;
}

/** A provider that could not be asked is verify_unavailable (503): the user tries again later. Anything else is a bug and stays a 500. */
function unavailable(err: unknown): never {
  if (err instanceof VerifyUnavailable) throw new AuthError("verify_unavailable", 503);
  throw err;
}

/**
 * Has the provider text a code to the number. The answer is the same whether or not another account
 * holds the number: the conflict is reported only once the code has proved that the requester holds the
 * phone (verifyBadge), so this step tells nobody which numbers are registered. Every limit is counted
 * before the provider is asked, so a refused start costs no text; the number is never stored.
 */
export async function startBadge(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, input: BadgeStartRequest, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<{ flowId: string }> {
  const verify = provider(deps);
  // 3e (design, section 7.2): the badge is a public mark, which a suspended account cannot ask for. A courtesy read, so
  // that no code is texted to it; the write in verifyBadge decides.
  if (await deps.profiles.suspended(session.userId)) throw new AuthError("account_suspended", 403);
  const hashed = phoneHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, input.phone);
  // The narrowest bucket first: a start the account's own limit refuses is not counted against the address or the
  // instance, so one account cannot spend their allowance with starts it was never going to get.
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `badge-start:${session.userId}`, BADGE_STARTS_PER_HOUR, HOUR);
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `badge-start:ip:${ctx.ipHash}`, BADGE_STARTS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR, HOUR);
  // Per number too, whoever asks, so one phone cannot be texted more than three times an hour through many accounts.
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `badge-start:phone:${hashed}`, BADGE_STARTS_PER_HOUR, HOUR);
  // The ceiling last, so it counts only starts every other bucket let through.
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, "badge-start:all", BADGE_STARTS_PER_DAY, 24 * HOUR);
  const { reference } = await verify.start(input.phone).catch(unavailable);
  const flowId = randomToken();
  const pending: PendingBadge = { userId: session.userId, phoneHash: hashed, reference, expiresAt: deps.now().getTime() + CODE_TTL_MS };
  await deps.kv.set(badgeKey(flowId), JSON.stringify(pending), CODE_TTL_MS);
  return { flowId };
}

/**
 * Checks the code with the provider. Attempts are counted before the provider is asked, as the email
 * codes count theirs, with the store's atomic counter: concurrent requests each get their own count, so
 * a flow takes at most five codes whatever the provider answers and however many requests arrive at
 * once. On success the account's phone hash is written first (the partial unique index on it decides
 * conflicts, so a number another account verified is phone_in_use here and only here), then the
 * profile's verified_at, and the account is told.
 */
export async function verifyBadge(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, input: BadgeVerifyRequest): Promise<BadgeVerifyResponse> {
  const verify = provider(deps);
  const key = badgeKey(input.flowId);
  const raw = await deps.kv.get(key);
  const pending = raw ? (JSON.parse(raw) as PendingBadge) : null;
  // A flow another account started, an unknown one and one whose ten minutes passed are all no code at all,
  // settled before an attempt is counted: nobody can spend another account's attempts. The store drops the
  // state itself at the end of the ten minutes; a straggler it still holds is treated like a flow that is gone.
  if (!pending || pending.userId !== session.userId) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  if (pending.expiresAt <= deps.now().getTime()) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  // The counter's life starts at the first attempt and is never extended; it outlives the state by at most ten minutes.
  const attempts = await deps.kv.incr(badgeAttemptsKey(input.flowId), CODE_TTL_MS);
  if (attempts > MAX_CODE_ATTEMPTS) throw new AuthError("too_many_attempts", 429);

  const outcome = await verify.check(pending.reference, input.code).catch(unavailable);
  if (outcome === "invalid_code") throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  if (outcome === "code_expired") {
    // The provider has closed the request, so no code can be checked against it any more: the owner starts again.
    await deps.kv.del(key);
    throw new AuthError("code_expired", 400);
  }
  // The code was right and the provider has spent it: whatever happens next, this flow is over.
  await deps.kv.del(key);
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  try {
    await deps.repo.setPhoneHash(user.id, pending.phoneHash);
  } catch (err) {
    if (isUniqueViolation(err)) throw new AuthError("phone_in_use", 409);
    throw err;
  }
  if (!(await deps.profiles.setVerified(user.id, deps.now()))) {
    // 3e: the one predicate refused the badge's write (a suspension started meanwhile): the phone hash written a moment
    // before is put back as it was read, so the account holds nothing of a badge it was refused. An account that already
    // had a badge keeps the number behind it (3e's review, access3): clearing it would leave the badge public with no
    // number, and free that number for another account's badge.
    await deps.repo.setPhoneHash(user.id, user.phoneHash);
    throw new AuthError("account_suspended", 403);
  }
  await notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "badge_verified");
  // No metadata: the event log never holds the number, not even hashed, since the hash leaves the account with the badge.
  await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: user.id, type: "badge_verified", deviceId: session.deviceId });
  return { verified: true };
}

/**
 * Drops the badge: the phone hash and verified_at are cleared, the account is told and the event
 * recorded. Without a badge nothing is said or recorded, but both columns are cleared anyway, which also
 * finishes a removal that stopped between its two writes. Works with the provider off, so turning it
 * off strands nobody.
 */
export async function removeBadge(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session): Promise<void> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  const held = user.phoneHash !== null;
  await deps.repo.setPhoneHash(user.id, null);
  await deps.profiles.setVerified(user.id, null);
  if (!held) return;
  await notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "badge_removed");
  await deps.repo.appendEvent({ userId: user.id, type: "badge_removed", deviceId: session.deviceId });
}

import type { DeleteConfirmRequest, DeleteStartResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AuthError, type AuthDeps, type RequestContext } from "../context";
import { randomToken } from "../crypto";
import { HOUR, enforceLimit } from "../limits";
import type { Session } from "../sessions";
import { CODE_TTL_MS, checkEmailCode, emailCodeHash, flowKey, newEmailCode, sendCode } from "./email";
import { noticeTime, notifyAccount } from "./notify";

export const DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR = 3;

/** The deletion a code is out for: kept under the hashed flow id until the code is entered or expires. */
export interface PendingDeletion {
  userId: string;
}

/**
 * Mails the deletion code to the account's own address (1b design, section 7.6): the second of the
 * three guards, after the fresh session the route demands and before the handle the owner types. The
 * code row carries the owner, so no other account can spend it.
 */
export async function startDeletion(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<DeleteStartResponse> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  await enforceLimit(deps.kv, `delete-start:${user.id}`, DELETE_STARTS_PER_HOUR, HOUR);
  const flowId = randomToken();
  const code = newEmailCode();
  await deps.repo.createEmailCode({
    flowId,
    email: user.email,
    userId: user.id,
    purpose: "delete_account",
    codeHash: emailCodeHash(deps.config.authHmacKey, flowId, code),
    expiresAt: new Date(deps.now().getTime() + CODE_TTL_MS),
    ipHash: ctx.ipHash,
  });
  const pending: PendingDeletion = { userId: user.id };
  await deps.kv.set(flowKey(flowId), JSON.stringify(pending), CODE_TTL_MS);
  await sendCode(deps, { to: user.email, template: "delete_account_code", data: { code } });
  return { flowId };
}

/**
 * Writes the cache tombstones of sessions the database has just revoked, so a cached copy cannot serve
 * them for the rest of its minute. Best effort: the rows are revoked whatever happens here, so a failure
 * only lets a cached copy live out that minute, and the account is not left half gone because the cache
 * was unreachable.
 */
async function tombstoneQuietly(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, sessionIds: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
  try {
    await deps.sessions.tombstone(sessionIds);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, userId }, "account deletion: the session tombstones could not be written; the sessions are revoked in the database");
  }
}

/**
 * The auth side of a deletion, step 1 of section 7.6: the typed handle must be the account's own,
 * then the code must be right; then, in one transaction, the account is marked deleted (every lookup
 * treats the row as absent from here, so no request can succeed against it while the purge runs),
 * every session revoked, its devices, codes and passkeys deleted, its WebAuthn user handle cleared and
 * the event recorded; then the revoked sessions get their tombstones, so the cache cannot revive one,
 * and the account is told. Nothing after the transaction can fail the request: the account is gone
 * once it commits. The row itself is anonymised by finishPurge, once the account module has purged the
 * other schemas.
 */
export async function confirmDeletion(deps: AuthDeps, session: Session, input: DeleteConfirmRequest): Promise<void> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(session.userId);
  if (!user) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
  // The handle is the third guard, compared in any case and checked before the code, so a slip of the fingers costs no attempt on it.
  const profile = await deps.profiles.find(user.id);
  if (!profile || profile.handle.toLowerCase() !== input.handle.toLowerCase()) throw new AuthError("invalid_request", 400, "handle_mismatch");
  const row = await deps.repo.findEmailCode(input.flowId);
  // A code from another account's deletion, or from any other flow, is no code at all, settled before an attempt is counted.
  if (row?.purpose !== "delete_account" || row.userId !== user.id) throw new AuthError("invalid_code", 400);
  await checkEmailCode(deps, row, input.flowId, input.code);
  // Taken, not read: whatever happens next, this flow is over and the code is spent.
  if (!(await deps.kv.take(flowKey(input.flowId)))) throw new AuthError("code_expired", 400);

  const revoked = await deps.repo.takeDown(user.id, deps.now(), session.deviceId);
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, user.id, revoked);
  // Told once the account is gone, and never before: a take-down that failed leaves the account as it was. The address
  // still belongs to the row until finishPurge; best effort, since no mail failure may keep an account its owner has given up.
  await notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "account_deleted");
}

/**
 * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.8 step 3): the take-down of an account whose termination is final for its author, as the
 * system, without a session or a code. As confirmDeletion does: the account's row is read first with its address, then
 * the account is marked deleted with every session revoked and the event written, in one transaction; the revoked
 * sessions get their tombstones; and only after that commit the address read before gets termination_final, best
 * effort, in place of account_deleted, with the decision's day and, when images of the account stay sealed, its
 * sentence about them. It does nothing a second time: an account already marked deleted (gone from every lookup) is
 * left as it is, with no event and no mail, and the answer is false; true only for the take-down this call made. The
 * address stays on the row until finishPurge, so nothing is lost by mailing after the commit.
 *
 * The mail is started and not waited for (3e's review, database3): the moderation module's take-down calls this while its
 * own transaction holds the account's profile FOR UPDATE, and a relay that stalls would hold that row, and every like,
 * repost and reply of the account's posts behind it, for as long as the relay. notifyAccount logs a failure itself and
 * never throws.
 */
export async function takeDownTerminated(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string, facts: { decidedAt: Date; imagesSealed: boolean }): Promise<boolean> {
  const user = await deps.repo.findUserById(userId);
  if (!user) return false;
  const revoked = await deps.repo.takeDownTerminated(user.id, deps.now());
  if (revoked === null) return false;
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, user.id, revoked);
  void notifyAccount(deps, user.email, "termination_final", { decided: noticeTime(facts.decidedAt), imagesSealed: String(facts.imagesSealed) });
  return true;
}

/**
 * Step 4 of section 7.6, which the purge job runs for every account left half deleted: the rows of
 * step 1 again (sessions still live revoked with their tombstones, devices, codes and passkeys deleted,
 * the WebAuthn user handle cleared), for an account marked deleted without the rest, then the row
 * anonymised and marked purged. Both parts change nothing for an account that is live or already
 * purged, so the job can repeat it after any failure.
 */
export async function finishPurge(deps: AuthDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  const revoked = await deps.repo.finishTakeDown(userId, deps.now());
  await tombstoneQuietly(deps, userId, revoked);
  await deps.repo.finishPurge(userId, deps.now());
}

 * two concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

export function createAuthRepo(db: Db) {
  return {
    // ------------------------------------------------------------ users

    async findUserByEmail(email: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(users)
        .where(and(sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${email})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    async findUserById(id: string): Promise<UserRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(users)
        .where(and(eq(users.id, id), isNull(users.deletedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** The email is already verified (the user proved it with a code) and the age check has passed. */
    async createUser(input: { email: string; termsVersion: string; now: Date }): Promise<UserRow> {
      const [row] = await db
        .insert(users)
        .values({
          email: input.email,
          emailVerifiedAt: input.now,
          ageConfirmedAt: input.now,
          termsVersion: input.termsVersion,
          termsAcceptedAt: input.now,
        })
        .returning();
      return row!;
    },

    async markOnboarded(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ onboardedAt: now }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * Moves the account to an address its owner just proved with a code, so it is verified as of now.
     * When another row holds the address, in any case, the unique index on lower(email) raises the
     * driver's unique violation; the flow reports that as email_in_use.
     */
    async changeEmail(userId: string, email: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ email, emailVerifiedAt: now }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * The keyed hash of the phone number behind the verified badge, or null to drop it. When another row
     * holds the same hash, the partial unique index on phone_hash raises the driver's unique violation;
     * the flow reports that as phone_in_use.
     */
    async setPhoneHash(userId: string, phoneHash: string | null): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ phoneHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Setting or clearing a password also clears any password lockout. */
    async setPasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string | null, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ passwordHash, passwordChangedAt: now, failedLogins: 0, lockedUntil: null })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Replaces the hash only, after a sign-in verified the password against older parameters. */
    async replacePasswordHash(userId: string, passwordHash: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ passwordHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async setPasswordFailures(userId: string, failedLogins: number, lockedUntil: Date | null): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ failedLogins, lockedUntil }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async enableTotp(userId: string, input: { secretEnc: string; recoveryCodesHash: string[]; now: Date }): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpSecretEnc: input.secretEnc, totpEnabledAt: input.now, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: input.recoveryCodesHash })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async disableTotp(userId: string): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] })
        .where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** The same secret re-encrypted with the current key; nothing else about MFA changes. */
    async setTotpSecretEnc(userId: string, totpSecretEnc: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ totpSecretEnc }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    async setRecoveryCodes(userId: string, recoveryCodesHash: string[]): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ recoveryCodesHash }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /** Claims a TOTP time step. False when this step or a later one was already used. */
    async claimTotpStep(userId: string, step: number): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ totpLastStep: step })
        .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), or(isNull(users.totpLastStep), lt(users.totpLastStep, step))))
        .returning({ id: users.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /** Removes one recovery-code hash. False when it is not (or no longer) present. */
    async consumeRecoveryCodeHash(userId: string, codeHash: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(users)
        .set({ recoveryCodesHash: sql`array_remove(${users.recoveryCodesHash}, ${codeHash})` })
        .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), sql`${codeHash} = ANY(${users.recoveryCodesHash})`))
        .returning({ id: users.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    async setRole(userId: string, role: UserRole): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ role }).where(eq(users.id, userId));
    },

    /**
     * A role change (3a design, section 7) in one transaction: the account's row is locked first, FOR NO KEY UPDATE (the
     * lock the role's update would take, and the one every writer of staff rows takes first, so none of them can wait on
     * another in a circle); the role is set, every session and every staff session revoked and every unused enrolment link
     * deleted, so the new role applies at once and no link issued before enrols anything. A change to user also revokes
     * every staff key, with a staff_key_revoked event each: a person made staff again enrols new keys. Last, through
     * auth.append_audit, each revocation's audit row and then the role_granted row, which hold the audit chain's head until
     * the commit, so the change and its record commit together or not at all. Only the command line calls this, and it
     * waits at most 10 seconds for a lock: an API that holds the head or the row open cannot stall it for longer, and one
     * that times out has changed nothing. The cache tombstones and the mail are not the database's to write, so the caller
     * does them after the commit with what this answers; undefined when no live account has the address.
     *
     * 3e (design, section 7.16): no suspended account becomes staff. For a promotion, auth.account_standing is asked in a
     * statement of its own after the row's lock: a deciding transaction reads the same row FOR SHARE, so it either waited
     * for this one and then meets staff_target, or committed first and is read here. When the account holds a standing
     * suspension, termination or restriction of reporting nothing is changed and the answer is "standing".
     */
    async changeRole(email: string, role: UserRole, audit: { actorId: string; now: Date }): Promise<RoleChange | "standing" | undefined> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
        const [account] = await tx
          .select({ id: users.id, email: users.email, role: users.role })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(sql`lower(${users.email}) = lower(${email})`, isNull(users.deletedAt)))
          .limit(1)
          .for("no key update");
        if (!account) return undefined;
        if (role !== "user") {
          const [standing] = await tx.execute<{ held: boolean }>(sql`select auth.account_standing(${account.id}::uuid) as held`);
          // Nothing was written: the transaction ends with the row's lock and no audit row.
          if (standing!.held) return "standing";
        }
        await tx.update(users).set({ role }).where(eq(users.id, account.id));
        const revoked = await tx
          .update(sessions)
          .set({ revokedAt: audit.now })
          .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, account.id), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ id: sessions.id });
        const staff = await revokeStaffAccess(tx, account.id, audit.now, { keys: role === "user", enrollments: "unused", via: "role_change" });
        await appendKeyRevocations(tx, audit.actorId, staff, "role_change");
        await appendAudit(tx, {
          actorId: audit.actorId,
          action: "role_granted",
          targetType: "user",
          targetId: account.id,
          // A role change deletes open links only, so every link it deleted was one it cancelled.
          metadata: { from: account.role, to: role, via: "cli", staffSessionsRevoked: staff.staffSessionsRevoked, enrollmentsDeleted: staff.enrollmentsCancelled },
        });
        return {
          userId: account.id,
          email: account.email,
          previousRole: account.role,
          sessionIds: revoked.map((row) => row.id),
          staffSessionsRevoked: staff.staffSessionsRevoked,
          enrollmentsDeleted: staff.enrollmentsCancelled,
          keysRevoked: staff.keys.map(({ id, name }) => ({ id, name })),
        };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ deletion

    /**
     * Marks the row deleted and nothing else: from now on every lookup above treats it as absent. Once only; a
     * later call changes nothing. A deletion goes through takeDown; this is the state a take-down that stopped
     * after the mark would leave, which finishTakeDown completes.
     */
    async markDeleted(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)));
    },

    /**
     * Step 1 of a deletion (1b design, section 7.6) in one transaction: the row is marked deleted, every live
     * session revoked, every device, code and passkey deleted, the WebAuthn user handle cleared, the account's staff
     * keys and staff sessions revoked, its enrolment links deleted and its keys blanked (3a design, section 7), and the
     * account_deleted event appended; last, the audit rows of the staff side, with the account as their actor, since its
     * owner asked for the deletion. Either all of it lands or none of it does, so a failure leaves a live account with its
     * sessions, never a deleted one with sessions, devices, passkeys or staff keys that nothing would remove. Answers the
     * ids of the sessions it revoked, for the cache tombstones, which are not the database's to write.
     */
    async takeDown(userId: string, now: Date, deviceId: string | null): Promise<string[]> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)));
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId, metadata: {} });
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, userId, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /**
     * 3e (design, sections 5 and 7.8): the take-down of a terminated account, as the system and not its owner. In one
     * transaction, as takeDown: the row marked deleted, step 1's rows, the account_deleted event (its metadata says that a
     * final termination took it down), and last the staff side's audit rows with the server as their actor. Only for a row
     * that this call marks: one already marked deleted (a round whose purge failed after the take-down, or the owner's own
     * deletion) is left as it is, nothing is written and the answer is null. Else the ids of the sessions it revoked.
     */
    async takeDownTerminated(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string[] | null> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        const marked = await tx.update(users).set({ deletedAt: now }).where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt))).returning({ id: users.id });
        if (marked.length === 0) return null;
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({ userId, type: "account_deleted", deviceId: null, metadata: { terminated: true } });
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /**
     * The rows of step 1 again (the sessions, devices, codes and passkeys, the WebAuthn user handle and the staff rows), for
     * a row marked deleted and not purged yet: a take-down that stopped after the mark, or a session that a sign-in already
     * past its lookup created after it. Nothing for a live or a purged row. The account_deleted event is not appended
     * again: the confirmation that recorded it is the only one there was. The staff side's audit rows are written, last,
     * for what this run revoked, with the server as their actor: the purge job finishes the take-down, no person.
     */
    async finishTakeDown(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        // The account's row first, as every writer of staff rows takes it (3a design, section 7).
        const [row] = await tx
          .select({ id: users.id })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)))
          .for("no key update");
        if (!row) return [];
        const taken = await takeDownRows(tx, userId, now);
        await appendTakeDownAudit(tx, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID, userId, taken.staff);
        return taken.sessionIds;
      });
    },

    /** Deleted accounts whose row the purge has not anonymised yet, oldest deletion first, at most 100 a round. */
    async pendingPurges(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: users.id })
        .from(users)
        .where(and(isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)))
        .orderBy(users.deletedAt, users.id)
        .limit(100);
      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
    },

    /**
     * The last step of a deletion: the address becomes deleted:<id> (unique, and never a real address),
     * every credential and personal fact is cleared, and purged_at says it is done. Only a deleted row
     * not purged yet is written, so a second call, or a call for a live account, changes nothing.
     */
    async finishPurge(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(users)
        .set({
          email: `deleted:${userId}`,
          emailVerifiedAt: null,
          passwordHash: null,
          totpSecretEnc: null,
          totpEnabledAt: null,
          recoveryCodesHash: [],
          phoneHash: null,
          ageConfirmedAt: null,
          termsVersion: null,
          termsAcceptedAt: null,
          purgedAt: now,
        })
        .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNotNull(users.deletedAt), isNull(users.purgedAt)));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ lockdown

    /**
     * The lockdown (1c design, sections 2 and 7.6) in one transaction, as takeDown is one: every live session
     * revoked, every device revoked (so the next sign-in on any of them counts as a new device), the password
     * cleared as setPasswordHash clears it, the passkeys in reach removed, two-factor turned off as disableTotp
     * does when it was enabled at or after `since`, and the caller's event appended with what was done. Either
     * all of it lands or none of it does: the link that started it is spent by then, so a lockdown that stopped
     * halfway could not be asked for again, and would be on no record. The user row is locked first, as takeDown
     * and a registration take it first, so none of the three can wait on another in a circle, and two-factor is
     * read from the locked row. Answers the ids of the sessions it revoked, for the cache tombstones, which are
     * not the database's to write.
     */
    async lockDown(userId: string, input: LockDownInput): Promise<LockDownOutcome> {
      return db.transaction(async (tx) => {
        // An account that is gone has no two-factor to clear; its rows, if any are left, are still locked down below.
        const [locked] = await tx
          .select({ totpEnabledAt: users.totpEnabledAt })
          .from(users)
          .where(and(eq(users.id, userId), isNull(users.deletedAt)))
          .for("update");
        const revoked = await tx
          .update(sessions)
          .set({ revokedAt: input.now })
          .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, userId), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
          .returning({ id: sessions.id });
        await tx.update(devices).set({ revokedAt: input.now }).where(and(eq(devices.userId, userId), isNull(devices.revokedAt)));
        // The user's passkeys from `since` on, plus any of theirs the caller names; a named passkey of another account is not the caller's to remove and stays.
        const reach = input.passkeyIds.length > 0 ? or(gte(passkeys.createdAt, input.since), inArray(passkeys.id, [...input.passkeyIds])) : gte(passkeys.createdAt, input.since);
        const removed = await tx
          .delete(passkeys)
          .where(and(eq(passkeys.userId, userId), reach))
          .returning({ id: passkeys.id });
        const totpCleared = locked !== undefined && locked.totpEnabledAt !== null && locked.totpEnabledAt.getTime() >= input.since.getTime();
        await tx
          .update(users)
          .set({
            passwordHash: null,
            passwordChangedAt: input.now,
            failedLogins: 0,
            lockedUntil: null,
            ...(totpCleared ? { totpSecretEnc: null, totpEnabledAt: null, totpLastStep: null, recoveryCodesHash: [] } : {}),
          })
          .where(eq(users.id, userId));
        const passkeysRemoved = removed.map((row) => row.id);
        await tx.insert(authEvents).values({
          userId,
          type: input.event.type,
          deviceId: input.event.deviceId,
          ipHash: input.event.ipHash,
          metadata: { ...input.event.metadata, passkeysRemoved, totpCleared, passwordCleared: true },
        });
        return { sessionIds: revoked.map((row) => row.id), passkeysRemoved, totpCleared };
      });
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ email codes

    async createEmailCode(input: {
      flowId: string;
      email: string;
      userId: string | null;
      purpose: EmailCodePurpose;
      codeHash: string;
      expiresAt: Date;
      ipHash: string | null;
    }): Promise<void> {
      await db.insert(emailCodes).values(input);
    },

    async findEmailCode(flowId: string): Promise<EmailCodeRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db.select().from(emailCodes).where(eq(emailCodes.flowId, flowId)).limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** Increments the attempt counter atomically and returns the new value. */
    async addCodeAttempt(id: string): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = await db
        .update(emailCodes)
        .set({ attempts: sql`${emailCodes.attempts} + 1` })
        .where(eq(emailCodes.id, id))
        .returning({ attempts: emailCodes.attempts });
      return row?.attempts ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER;
    },

    /** Marks a code used. False when it was already used, so a code works exactly once. */
    async consumeEmailCode(id: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(emailCodes)
        .set({ consumedAt: now })
        .where(and(eq(emailCodes.id, id), isNull(emailCodes.consumedAt)))
        .returning({ id: emailCodes.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ devices

    async findDevice(userId: string, deviceHash: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select()
        .from(devices)
        .where(and(eq(devices.userId, userId), eq(devices.deviceHash, deviceHash), isNull(devices.revokedAt)))
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    /** The device by its row id, revoked or not: a session's device, whose platform names a passkey and whose label the passkey notices carry. */
    async findDeviceById(id: string): Promise<DeviceRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db.select().from(devices).where(eq(devices.id, id)).limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    async createDevice(input: { userId: string; deviceHash: string; label: string; platform: string; ipHash: string | null }): Promise<DeviceRow> {
      const [row] = await db.insert(devices).values(input).returning();
      return row!;
    },

    async touchDevice(id: string, ipHash: string | null, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(devices).set({ lastSeenAt: now, ipHash }).where(eq(devices.id, id));
    },

    /** A revoked device no longer carries live sessions and counts as new at its next sign-in. */
    async revokeDevice(id: string, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(devices).set({ revokedAt: now }).where(and(eq(devices.id, id), isNull(devices.revokedAt)));
    },

    /** The user's devices that are not revoked, oldest first, for the data export; a revoked one stands for nothing of the account's any more. */
    async listDevices(userId: string): Promise<{ label: string | null; platform: string; firstSeenAt: Date; lastSeenAt: Date }[]> {
      return db
        .select({ label: devices.label, platform: devices.platform, firstSeenAt: devices.firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt: devices.lastSeenAt })
        .from(devices)
        .where(and(eq(devices.userId, userId), isNull(devices.revokedAt)))
        .orderBy(devices.firstSeenAt, devices.id);
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ sessions

    /**
     * A new session with the factors its sign-in proved (kind to epoch milliseconds from the flows' clock) and the passkey
     * that started it, if one did. The reauth time is the latest of the factors, which is what freshness is read from. A row
     * without factors, as migration 0010 left the sessions from before it, re-authenticates before its next sensitive action.
     */
    async createSession(input: {
      id: string;
      userId: string;
      deviceId: string;
      now: Date;
      expiresAt: Date;
      absoluteExpiresAt: Date;
      factors?: Record<string, number>;
      passkeyId?: string | null;
    }): Promise<void> {
      const factors = input.factors ?? {};
      const times = Object.values(factors);
      await db.insert(sessions).values({
        id: input.id,
        userId: input.userId,
        deviceId: input.deviceId,
        createdAt: input.now,
        lastUsedAt: input.now,
        reauthAt: times.length > 0 ? new Date(Math.max(...times)) : input.now,
        expiresAt: input.expiresAt,
        absoluteExpiresAt: input.absoluteExpiresAt,
        factors,
        passkeyId: input.passkeyId ?? null,
      });
    },

    /** A session counts only when neither it, its device nor its user is revoked, deleted or expired. */
    async findActiveSession(id: string, now: Date): Promise<ActiveSessionRow | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .select({
          id: sessions.id,
          userId: sessions.userId,
          deviceId: sessions.deviceId,
          role: users.role,
          onboardedAt: users.onboardedAt,
          totpEnabledAt: users.totpEnabledAt,
          reauthAt: sessions.reauthAt,
          lastUsedAt: sessions.lastUsedAt,
          expiresAt: sessions.expiresAt,
          absoluteExpiresAt: sessions.absoluteExpiresAt,
          handle: sessions.handle,
          factors: sessions.factors,
          passkeyId: sessions.passkeyId,
        })
        .from(sessions)
        .innerJoin(users, eq(users.id, sessions.userId))
        .innerJoin(devices, eq(devices.id, sessions.deviceId))
        .where(
          and(
            eq(sessions.id, id),
            isNull(sessions.revokedAt),
            gt(sessions.expiresAt, now),
            gt(sessions.absoluteExpiresAt, now),
            isNull(users.deletedAt),
            isNull(devices.revokedAt),
          ),
        )
        .limit(1);
      return row;
    },

    async slideSession(id: string, expiresAt: Date, now: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db.update(sessions).set({ expiresAt, lastUsedAt: now }).where(eq(sessions.id, id));
    },

    /**
     * Records a factor the session proved at `at`: the kind's time is set or replaced, and reauth_at, the latest of
     * them, follows the write. The flows always pass their clock's now.
     */
    async writeFactor(id: string, kind: string, at: Date): Promise<void> {
      await db
        .update(sessions)
        .set({ factors: sql`${sessions.factors} || ${JSON.stringify({ [kind]: at.getTime() })}::jsonb`, reauthAt: at })
        .where(eq(sessions.id, id));
    },

    /**
     * Replaces the session's id, the token's hash, and nothing else, for a live session only: the handle, factors, reauth
     * time, passkey, device and expiries stay. False when the session is revoked or gone, so a rotation never revives one.
     * Nothing references sessions.id, so the primary key changes in place.
     */
    async rotateSession(id: string, newId: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(sessions)
        .set({ id: newId })
        .where(and(eq(sessions.id, id), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
        .returning({ id: sessions.id });
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * Revokes one session of this user, named by its handle: the id a rotation keeps, so a session listed before its
     * token rotated is still found. Answers the row's id as it is now, which its cached copy is keyed by; undefined
     * when the session does not belong to the user or is already revoked.
     */
    async revokeSession(handle: string, userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string | undefined> {
      const [row] = await db
        .update(sessions)
        .set({ revokedAt: now })
        .where(and(eq(sessions.handle, handle), eq(sessions.userId, userId), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
        .returning({ id: sessions.id });
      return row?.id;
    },

    /** Revokes every live session of the user and returns their ids (for cache invalidation). */
    async revokeAllSessions(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(sessions)
        .set({ revokedAt: now })
        .where(and(eq(sessions.userId, userId), isNull(sessions.revokedAt)))
        .returning({ id: sessions.id });
      return rows.map((r) => r.id);
    },

    async listActiveSessions(userId: string, now: Date): Promise<SessionListRow[]> {
      return db
        .select({
          id: sessions.id,
          handle: sessions.handle,
