```markdown
- **The take-down holds the terminating decision's row, not its case (5, the lock order, item 5 step 2; 7.8 step 3; 13 Task 4 item 2).** The design says that takeDownDue takes 'the case of the terminate's decision FOR UPDATE, profile before case as in every decision'. korbat_api has no UPDATE privilege on cases, so a row lock on a case is refused (permission denied for table cases), and granting one, or a definer function that locks the case, would be migration 0022, which this task may not add. takeDownDue therefore takes, after the profile, the terminating decision's own row FOR UPDATE (lockTerminatingDecision in standing-repo.ts): an appeal being filed inserts a row whose foreign key takes that decision row FOR KEY SHARE, so it either commits first and is read by the second terminations_due(), or waits until the take-down has committed. Because appeals_check reads the deadline before that foreign key lock, an appeal whose deadline check passed an instant before the deadline could still be in flight; the take-down therefore also requires that the decision became final at least TAKE_DOWN_SETTLE_MS (60 seconds, finalSettled) before it acts, longer than any bounded lock wait of an appeal. A termination is thus taken down in the first purge round at least a minute after it became final. If the case lock is wanted, 0022 can grant it and the decision row lock can stay as a second guard.
- **takeDown answers whether it took the account down (5, ModerationForAccount.takeDownDue).** The design types the callback as (account, facts) => Promise<void>. The code's TakeDown answers Promise<boolean>: AuthForAccount.takeDownTerminated answers true only when it marked the account deleted (the auth repository's new takeDownTerminated marks a row not yet marked, writes the account_deleted event with metadata { terminated: true } and the staff side's audit rows with the server as actor, and answers null for a row already marked), so terminated counts the take-downs made, and a round that meets an account already taken down (its purge failed after the take-down) counts nothing and sends no second termination_final.
- **A failed take-down is logged with its case, not the account (5, the lock order, item 5).** The design says such a failure 'is caught, logged with the account and counted in failed'. No log line may carry an account id, so the log line names the terminating decision's case (caseId), from which an operator finds the account.
- **The withdrawal's statement knows whether a reply was closed (10.2 StatementReversal; W.2 withdrawn).** W.2's withdrawn sentence says that the withdrawal is no decision on the person's reply only when they replied, and 10.2 gives the lift's reversal liftedKind, liftedDecidedAt, periodThen and replaced but not the reply. StatementReversal gains replyFiledAt (optional, null when no reply was filed), read in the correction's transaction, so the statement reads the same whenever it is rendered.
- **DecisionView.standing carries the period and the reply, not the measure's kind and days (9.2, 10.2).** The design's DecisionView.standing is read by the app for the block 'Where it stands now'. The code's DecisionStanding holds state, earliestStart, startsAt, endsAt, endedAt, endedBy, replaced, restsOn (each strike with its rule, decidedAt, countsUntil, state and overruledAt; a decision a measure at once rests on with state null), reply (filedAt, onTime, text, erasedAt, answeredAt, answeredBy) and replyOpen; the kind, the days and the basis are read from the statement's measures (standingMeasureOf in apps/app/src/lib/standing.ts), which never change, so they are not sent twice.
- **The Standing screen's rows carry their case (8.6, 10.3 StandingLists).** 10.3 lists caseId for noticesUndelivered and terminationsWaiting only, while 8.6 says each row ends in a link to its case where one exists. atThreeStrikes and reportingRecords rows also carry caseId, the account's open account case or null, so the console links it beside 'Open a case on this account'. reportingRecords is empty until Task 5 builds the view reporting_record.
- **The basis of a termination at once, for the preview (10.3 CaseStanding.basisDecidedAt).** Task 3 gave basisDecidedAt threat, terrorist and protective. A termination at once rests on two R5 decisions, and W.2's terminateAtOnce names both by their times, so basisDecidedAt gains threatRepeat { earlier, newer } (optional; null when the ground is not met), read by standingFacts beside atOnce, so the console's preview prints the sentence the statement will hold.
- **Appeals of a standing measure lead the first page (8.5, 10.3 AppealsPage).** The design says /appeals lists first the appeals of a decision that holds a running suspension or a termination, then the rest as D 8 orders them. pendingAppeals is paged by a cursor over D 8's order, so the first group is read in full on the first page (at most a page of them, rows marked standingFirst) and excluded from the cursor's pages; a later page carries the rest in D 8's order. More than a page of such appeals at once would leave the excess in D 8's place.
- **A strike's row in the console's preview may have no post time (W.2 restsOnEntry).** The design's restsOnEntry names each strike with the post it was given for. The console builds its preview from the case answer, whose strikes carry no post's creation time, so restsOnEntry takes postCreatedAt null and then leaves the bracket out; the statement the database stores always has it.
- **The app's times: a day for a name ending in On, a minute for one ending in At (9, 9.1 to 9.3).** The design says times are printed by standingTime. The code prints {earliestStart}, {startsAt}, {endsAt} and {appealUntil} with standingTime (the device's minute and the UTC minute) and the names that end in On ({repliedOn}, {liftedOn}, {endedOn}, {answeredOn}, {erasedOn}) with standingDay, as the strike's [strike.overruled] already does; [reply.sent.onTime] and [reply.sent.late] print the minute the reply was received.
- **Two sentences of 'Where it stands now' the table leaves open (9.2).** For an announced termination [now.announced] says only 'Starts on {startsAt}.' since a termination has no end; for a protective suspension whose basis broke while it ran, [now.basis.running] reads 'Ended on {endedOn}, because korbat lifted the seal it rested on.' (the design's replacement phrase does not occur in that sentence). The link to the decision that ended a measure is worded 'Read the decision that did this', and the reply's link to its answer 'Read the answer'.
- **The reply screen's sent notice takes the focus as a focusable alert (9.3, 9.8).** The design says the sentences after Send reply are a Notice that receives focus. ui.tsx's Notice takes no ref, so the reply screen draws the same box as a focusable View with role alert and moves the focus to it once the answer arrives.
- **A locking statement is judged before it waits behind a holder that changes nothing (7.2 rule 1, 11 'A write is judged when it gets the row', 12.3 LAB C1).** The design says that a transaction that began before a start and waited for a lock is judged when it gets the row. Lab C1 on the real code confirms this behind a holder that changes the profile row (PostgreSQL re-reads the row and computes the predicate again: 150 wave writes, 0 admitted), but behind a holder that only locks the row FOR UPDATE and changes nothing (a decision about the account whose measure leaves the profile's columns as they are, a late reply, the take-down), a SELECT ... FOR KEY SHARE computes its target list, and an UPDATE its WHERE, before it waits: 22 of 72 such writes, judged before the start, committed after it, the latest 339 ms after, bounded by the holder's time. No write was judged at or after a start, so invariant 10 as 11 words it holds; the sentence 'judged when it gets the row' holds only behind a changing holder. Closing the gap would mean judging after the lock in a statement of its own (Task 3's write paths) and is left to the design's owner.
- **Labs C and D run in a block of their own with the notices world (12.3).** Labs C1, C2 and D are added to apps/api/test/lab/standing.lab.ts in a describe of their own, which builds the notices world so that each announced suspension's notice is mailed and its start fixed, then brings the start 1.5 s ahead with ageStandingForTest. C2's predicate reading now() is copied into the lab as nowGatedWrite. They run alone with -t 'labs? [CD]'; LAB_C_SUBJECTS (25) and LAB_D_SUBJECTS (60) size them as the design's labs. The run of this task: C1 25 starts, 3,245 free writes and 150 wave writes, 0 admitted at or after a start, 0 refused before one; C2 102 of 150 wave writes admitted after the start, the latest 311 ms after it; D 60 replies from 275 ms before to 307 ms after the start (29 on time, 31 late), on_time equal to filed_at < start in all 60, 10,285 writes, none refused before a start or after an on-time reply, none admitted after the start of a late one.
- **The counts' migration number (6, The numbers; 6.3).** The migration the design numbers 0021 `reporting_counts` is `0022_reporting_counts.sql`: 3c's last task added 0019, so every migration of 3e is one number higher.
- **The rows of reporting_record (6.3).** The view lists an account that holds a tally or a mark that counts within the frame; an account with neither has no row, and every reader takes it as 0 reports and 0 marked reports. Its frame is the one decision_actions_check's restriction counts by: a UTC day later than today, by `now()`, less `report_frame_days`. It is written as one row set of account ids with a correlated count on each side, so a read for one account uses each table's index.
- **The warning's time in the case answer (8.1, 10.3).** `CaseStanding.reporting` also carries `warnedAt`, the warning decision's instant, beside the day `warnedOn`: the console's preview of a restriction prints the warning it follows to the minute ({warnedAt}, W.2), and a day cannot.
- **The marks the drafts list (10.3, W.5).** `CaseStanding.reporting.marked` holds one row a mark that counts (`ref`, `position`, `sentOn`, `markedOn`) and also `sinceWarning`, true when its report was sent after korbat told the account of its warning, so the restriction's draft lists only those; the list holds at most 100 rows. {marked} names each report once, with all its marked items: "report N-... of 2026-09-03 (items 1 and 3)".
- **What markable means (10.3).** `CaseItem.markable` is the item's own fact, whether or not it is answered: it is no re-examination and came from a `user` intake with a sender still known that alleges no illegality and is not on the path for child sexual abuse material. The console offers the tick box only beside the items a final "No breach" decision made now would answer; the database's check refuses every other mark.
- **The rows of the person's list (9.4, 10.2).** `AuthorCaseRow` gains two optional members: `reportingDays`, the days of the decision's restriction of reporting, and `endedStanding`, the kinds whose basis a reversal of this decision broke (a restriction lifted by its own reversal before is left out). The app words the restriction's row, "your reports under the rules restricted for {days} days", and "a restriction of your reports that rested on it ended"; the suspension's "a suspension that rested on it ended" stays for the task that words Task 4's rows.
- **What a lift of a reporting measure names (10.2, W.2).** `StatementReversal.liftedKind` takes `warn_reporting` and `restrict_reporting` too, and on a lifted restriction `periodThen` says whether its days still ran (`running`, from its decision) or had run out (`ended`, with its decision's time plus its days as its end), which `reportingLifted` prints. A restriction in `endedStanding` carries the same two states.
- **DecisionView.reportingStanding is optional (10.2).** The member is nullable and optional, so a view built before Task 5 still parses; the API always sends it, null for a decision without a restriction. For a restriction that ran its days the state is `ended` and the sentence prints its end as decided (`until`).
- **The order of the reporting records (8.6).** "Each newest first" reads, for the reporting records, as the account with the newest mark that counts first.
- **The routes' list after Task 5 (7.1 item 2; 13).** `ROUTE_KINDS` holds all 22 kinds and `refuseUnopened` no longer reads the marks: the database's check of every mark and decision_holds at commit decide whether a mark can stand. `DecideOptions.allKinds` now changes nothing; the fixtures still pass it.
- **The words the design leaves out (8.4, 8.7).** The composer's mark fieldset is "Reports this decision answers" with a tick box "Manifestly unfounded: item {n}" for each item; the case page says "Marked manifestly unfounded" beside an item whose mark stands and "Mark withdrawn" beside one a correction withdrew; "Withdraw this decision's marks" shows, in place of a preview, "No statement is sent: withdrawing marks changes nothing for the author of what was reported, and the people who reported see it on their own lists." The reversals read "Lift the warning about reporting" and "Lift the restriction of reporting". A restriction's days default to `report_restrict_days` when it is chosen.
- **The preview of a lift of a warning (8.3, 8.7).** The console's preview of a review or a correction that lifts a warning does not print basisEndedReporting for the restriction that rests on it: that restriction's decision lies in another case, which the case answer does not carry. [review.warning] says beside the reversal that the restriction ends when the key confirms, and the statement the person receives carries the paragraph, read from the ledger.
- **How the tests meet the frame and clean the tallies (12).** `ageStandingForTest` also moves the reports the account sent (`intakes.received_at`) and its tallies, by the interval's whole days, so a report and its mark leave the frame together. Since every signed-in rule report leaves a tally, the cleanup lowers the tallies of the intakes it deletes (`untally`, in removeCasesIn and in the notices harness) and `removeFixtures` deletes the tallies of the profiles it removes; `scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs` deletes the doomed accounts' tallies only.
- **The job's timer reads EXPLORE_V2 (section 5).** Section 5 says that `social/explore.ts` holds only the job's timer and does not change. It changes by one name: its timer reads `refreshMinutes` from `EXPLORE_V1`, which 10.1 stops exporting, so it reads `EXPLORE_V2.refreshMinutes`, the same 5 minutes. Nothing else of the job changes.
- **A removal that ends its own case's withhold passes through visible (6.4; invariant 18).** 6.4 says that a move between `withheld` and `removed` writes none of the three columns. That holds for a move made by one call of `moderation_apply`, such as a removal reversed while another case's withhold stands, which the tests prove with committed decisions. The commonest path is not such a move: a final removal decided in the case whose interim withhold it ends runs `decisions_apply` first, which closes the case and derives the level (the withhold has ended, so the post is visible for that instant), and then `decision_actions_apply`, which derives it again with the removal. So `moderation_apply` writes `restored_at` and `explore_from` for the end of the withhold and then `hidden_at` anew, all at that transaction's `now()`. No other transaction sees the visible level, the span that ended and the one that starts meet at that instant, so `explore_from` stays `created_at` plus the ledger's hidden spans to the microsecond, and the next real restore overwrites `restored_at`. No reader reads the three columns of a post that is not visible. The rule is kept as 6.4 states it: telling such a pass from a real restore would need the values it overwrote.
- **The status judges a suspension at the database's clock (7.13 item 7).** The status answers `suspended` when the author's suspension runs at `clock_timestamp()`, read in the statement of `exploreFacts`, as `explorePage` and `listedInExplore` judge it, and not at the flow's request time `now`, so the status says why the page and the chip leave the post out. Its other rules still judge at `now` and at the ranking's time, and a round judges at its own `at`.
- **A post can come back before the next round (7.13 item 6).** 7.13 says that when a suspension ends the author's posts return with the next round, if still in their window. The page and the chip judge the author at each read against the newest ranking, so a post that ranking holds comes back at the first read after the suspension ends. In practice that ranking was computed during the suspension and holds none of the author's posts, so they return with the next round; only a suspension that ends within the same refresh interval as the ranking that listed the post (one lifted at once, say) shows the post again at the next read. How Explore works and the status line promise no earlier than the next refresh, which stays true.
- **The retention migration's number (6, The numbers; 6.5).** The migration the design numbers 0023 `standing_retention` is `0024_standing_retention.sql`: 3c's review added `0019_redaction_scope.sql`, so each of 3e's five migrations is one higher (`0020_fearless_absorbing_man.sql`, `0021_standing_ledger.sql`, `0022_reporting_counts.sql`, `0023_explore_resume.sql`, `0024_standing_retention.sql`), and `--upgrade-from` names 19.
- **The frame's boundary (6.5, 7.14).** `forget_report_counts()` deletes exactly the complement of `reporting_record`'s frame: every mark, withdrawn ones included, whose `(reported_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date` is at or before today's UTC day minus `report_frame_days`, and every tally of such a day. A report sent on the last day outside the frame goes with its tally; one sent the day after stays on both sides, so what the warning and the restriction read is the same before and after the step.
- **The two steps' place and the round's report (7.14).** The steps run after `statements` and before `access_log`, each one call through `inStep` with an id-less audit row (`step`, null ids, `count`) when it changed something. `RetentionReport` gains `replies` (the replies whose text was erased) and `reportCounts` (the marks and tallies deleted), and the round's log line carries both.
- **RETENTION's three members (10.1, W.7).** `replyText` is the phrase the terms print, 'until korbat has answered it and its decision can no longer be appealed'; `reportCountDays` is `STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays`; `standingRecord` is `{ strikeDays, ladderMemoryDays, warningDays }`, each read from `STANDING_RULES`, in place of W.7's string 'kept; counted for {strike_days}, {ladder_memory_days} and {report_frame_days} days'. `RETENTION` held numbers only, and the terms' table test names every number of it by its path: so the record's three periods are numbers the table holds to their sentences in 'Your data', and the reply's period is a phrase the test holds to its sentence and changes in the test with other constants, as it changes a rule's text. `STANDING_RULES` is declared before `RETENTION` in `moderation.ts`, which reads it.
- **The terms' sentence on a reply's text (W.7, 'Your data').** It reads 'The text of a reply to a suspension is kept {RETENTION.replyText}; a reply that is not answered yet is never erased.' in place of '... is erased once korbat has answered it and its decision can no longer be appealed; ...': the same rule, printed from the constant.
- **Numbers the terms work out from a constant (W.7, 12.2).** `reportWarnShare` is printed 'half' for 0.5 and as a percentage otherwise; 'at least two earlier strikes' prints `ladderStrikes` minus one; 'three such suspensions' and 'after three suspensions' print the number of the ladder's rungs (`ladderDays.length`); 'six months' prints `APPEAL_MONTHS`. The table test holds each, and its run with other constants keeps arrays as arrays and counts those worked-out values among the constants' digits.
- **What each new measure does, in How moderators decide (W.7).** W.7 has no words for them, so `MEASURE_MEANINGS` gives: strike 'a mark on the account that restricts nothing by itself and counts toward a suspension, as Strikes says'; suspend 'for a number of days the account can no longer post, engage, follow, edit its profile or report under the rules, as Suspension and termination says'; terminate 'the account is suspended until the decision is final, and then deleted, as Suspension and termination says'; retire_handle 'the handle can be used by nobody again, and the profile shows a placeholder in its place, as Handles says'; warn_reporting 'a warning about reports that are manifestly unfounded, which restricts nothing, as Reporting in bad faith says'; restrict_reporting 'for a number of days korbat takes no report under its rules from the account, as Reporting in bad faith says'. Every kind of `MEASURES` is listed by the ledger's two marks, each meaning pointing to its section in words rather than in brackets, since the sentence already sets the meaning in brackets; `LISTED_TARGETS` and the test's `listedIn` are gone.
- **Where the four sections stand, and two sentences W.7 leaves as they were (W.7).** Strikes, Suspension and termination, Reporting in bad faith and Handles follow Appeals and come before Terrorist content. Appeals' first sentence reads 'If a final decision restricts your content or your account', since a standing measure restricts an account and can be appealed; W.7's paragraph on a reply and the six months joins Appeals before its last paragraph. The reporter-forgetting sentence gains its clause at its end: '..., while it can still be re-examined, except through the mark of a report found manifestly unfounded (Reporting in bad faith).' The Handles section names rule R4 as 'rule R4', without the rule's title.
- **ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE in the terms (W.7, 3c's section 12).** The paragraph after the outcome phrases says W.7's two sentences and quotes both phrases from the constant between them: when korbat's answer to a report about an account is a measure on that account, it tells the reporter that it took a measure, and not which or for how long, the answer adding `ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.measure`, or `ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.retired` when it retired the handle. The paragraph begins with no quotation mark, so it is no answer paragraph, and the table test holds it as it holds every outcome phrase. The placeholder's prefix in Handles is `RETIRED_HANDLE_PREFIX`.
- **The export's three members as built (W.8).** `standing` lists the account's `suspend`, `terminate`, `warn_reporting` and `restrict_reporting` rows, newest first: for a suspension or a termination `earliestStart` is the row's `starts_at` and `startsAt` and `endsAt` are its `suspension_periods` row (null with no start, `endsAt` null for a termination); for a warning `startsAt` is its decision and `endsAt` its end of counting cut to a lift; for a restriction `startsAt` is its start and `endsAt` its days' end cut to a lift and to a broken basis; `earliestStart` is null for the two reporting measures, `replaced` false unless a withdrawal signed it. `replies` are newest first. `reporting.days` lists every tally korbat holds for the account, newest day first, also one the retention job has not yet deleted; `marks` lists every mark, withdrawn ones included, newest report first, with `counts` as `markCounts` reads it; `markedReports` is `reporting_record`'s `unfounded`. An account module built without the moderation module writes empty lists and `frameDays` from `STANDING_RULES`.
- **text-verify and the marks korbat deletes (6.5, 3c's 7.13).** `forget_report_counts` and `forget_reporter` delete marks that a decision's params signed, so `staff.js text-verify` takes a signed mark with no row for no difference when korbat's own rules may have deleted it: its report was sent on a UTC day at or before the frame's boundary, or its intake names no sender any more. An intake whose record `erase_intake` erased also names no sender, so a mark deleted by hand from such a report is not told apart; a mark deleted while its report is in the frame and its sender known is still reported.
- **The smoke test's two steps (12.2, Smoke).** `/api/me` for the onboarded smoke account must answer `standing` deeply equal to `{ activeStrikes: 0, measure: null, reporting: null, handleRetired: false }` (compared with `isDeepStrictEqual`), and `/api/staff/standing` joins `caseRoutes`: 404 from Caddy on the app's site, 401 `staff_session_required` on the console's.
- **The README's 3e text and its docs test (13, Task 7).** The README describes 3e under Moderation in a paragraph that opens 'Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;' and ten bullets, before the runbook, and the runbook's bullets (a) to (h) stand together where 3c's handle bullet stood, which becomes (d). The Standing screen holds four lists; 'Replies to answer' stands on the queue screen (8.5), so bullet (a) reads the replies there first. `apps/admin/test/readme.test.ts` lists the bullets' titles, holds every number of that text to `STANDING_RULES` and `REPLY_AIM_HOURS` in its sentence, refuses any other run of digits, and checks that the lines 3e made false are gone. The hard gate already read 3f and 3d and is unchanged.
- **How the retention of 3e is tested (12).** `standing-retention.test.ts` runs as the migrator inside transactions that are rolled back, deciding through the module's own decide and moving the clock with `ageStandingForTest` on the transaction (its own transaction becomes a savepoint); the round's two steps run through `retentionRound` over that transaction with a media interface that drops and requests nothing, after a first round that clears whatever another suite left due. A reply filed after its decision became final is a reply to a termination at once, the one measure that has not ended six months on.
- **The review's migration (6, The numbers).** What the review of the built code upheld in the database is one hand-written migration the design does not name, `0025_standing_review.sql`: it replaces the view `reporting_record` (0022) and the functions `decision_actions_check`, `decision_holds`, `suspension_replies_check` (0021) and `erase_reply_statements` (0024), each stated whole from its newest text, and back-fills `report_tallies`.
- **The closing judgment (7.2 rule 2, 11.2 'A write is judged when it gets the row'; section 19's Task 4 bullet on lab C1).** 7.2 rule 2 says a write reads only columns of a profile row that its own statement locks or updates, never a second statement's. Every write of 7.3 that a suspension refuses now ends its transaction with one more read of the acting account's row by the clock, after every lock, insert and counter update: `closingJudgment(tx, account)` in `lib/standing.ts` (deleted, suspended, reports restricted), through `judgeActing` in the social repository (createPost after `within`, like, repost and bookmark after their counters, follow after its counters, changeHandle last), in `insertProcessing` after its insert, and in the intake of a signed-in report under a rule as its step 6 (account_suspended, then reporting_restricted). It rolls the write back. A locking statement computes its judgment before it waits, so behind a holder that only locks the row (a decision about the account), behind one that changes the other party's row (lockPair and lockLive project every row before locking), and behind a decision that holds the post FOR UPDATE (a foreign key or a counter), a write judged before a start committed after it; with the closing judgment none does. The read waits for nothing: the write holds the acting row at least FOR KEY SHARE until its commit, and every writer of a start takes that row FOR UPDATE first. 11.2's bullet is replaced: a write is judged when it gets its rows and again by its last statement, so none commits after a start that came before its end. Task 4's bullet that left the gap to the owner is closed.
- **The profile's edit, the badge and the upload (7.2's table).** `updateProfile` and `ProfileStore.setVerified(id, at)` are each a transaction: the row FOR NO KEY UPDATE in a statement of its own, then the UPDATE with the fragment in its WHERE, which, coming after the only wait, is the write's closing judgment. `insertProcessing` is a transaction of its one statement and the closing judgment. A deleted or suspended owner answers account_suspended, as the one statement did.
- **The bound of a starved lock (5, the lock order; 7.6 step 9; 7.8 step 3; 3c 7.5).** Wherever lock_timeout is the bound, `boundLockWaits` (a confirmed decision, a reveal, a staff session's revocation) and `boundWaits` (the reply, the take-down), the same length is set as the transaction's `statement_timeout`, in one `set_config` statement: lock_timeout is armed again at each wait of one statement, so a FOR UPDATE on a profile that others' likes keep out of reach with FOR KEY SHARE (each new one joins the holders without queueing behind it) waited as long as the likes kept coming (16 likers: 10.6 s; 24: past 120 s). `isBoundReached(err)` (55P03 or 57014) is retried, answered `late` or `service_unavailable` as a lock timeout was; the take-down's round counts it in `failed`. The starvation itself (liveness) is recorded for the owner, not removed.
- **No profile is held across a mail (5, the lock order, item 4; 7.8 step 3; 7.14 item 3).** `sendStatement` takes the decision's row (FOR NO KEY UPDATE, while its mail is owed), sends, and only then the subject's profile FOR NO KEY UPDATE, right before it records the outcome; `giveUpAnnounced` takes the decision's row, then the profile, then records. A deciding transaction takes the decisions it answers FOR KEY SHARE only, through its foreign key, so the new order meets no decision in the opposite order; the take-down, the only transaction that takes a profile and then a decision's row FOR UPDATE, only takes a termination whose period started, which an owed notice never gives. The auth module's `takeDownTerminated` starts `termination_final` without awaiting it (notifyAccount logs a failure itself), so the take-down's transaction, which holds the profile FOR UPDATE, never waits on the relay; the mail still goes only after the auth module's take-down committed. One cost of the order: when the profile stays held past the mail's lock wait after the send, the record is rolled back and the mail stays pending to be sent again, as after a crash between the relay and the record (the later start favours the person).
- **A notice whose measure was withdrawn is never sent (7.6, 7.14, 7.15).** `sendStatement`, after the decision's row is held, reads in a statement of its own whether a later decision lifted the statement's suspension or termination or a reversal broke its basis (`standingWithdrawn`); it then records the mail `failed` without sending it (the measure, lifted, fixes no start). Before, the dispatch's retry sent `suspension_announced` with an earliest start and an invitation to reply after the person had read `suspension_lifted`.
- **A mark counts only once its item's outcome is released (6.3, 7.9 step 3, 7.12, 8.4, W.8).** Before the daily release the person can neither read a mark nor ask for a re-examination of it. `reporting_record`, the restriction's inline count in `decision_actions_check` and the API's `markCounts` (so `reportingFacts`' counts and marked list, `reportingRecords`, the marked reports since a warning) count and list a mark only when `intake_items.outcome_sent_at` is set; the export (`exportedReporting`) lists only such marks, and `markedReports` follows the view. W.8's `markedAt` is kept to the second (the review's suggestion of a day was considered: a released mark is the person's own released outcome).
- **The tallies' back-fill (6.3).** 0022's trigger counts only reports received after it, so 0025 sets each account's tally of each UTC day within `report_frame_days` to at least the number of its signed-in rule reports of that day (`greatest` of the tally and the count, where the review's finder added the two), so a database that ran 0022 before this migration counts none twice and a second run changes nothing. Its test runs the migration's own statement over reports whose tallies were removed, as an upgrade meets them.
- **A withdrawal is an admin's, in the database too (7.6 step 12, 8.7).** `decision_holds` accepts a stored `replaced = true` only when the deciding account's auth role is admin, and raises `admin_required` otherwise; only the console enforced it before.
- **A reply after the take-down (6.2 suspension_replies_check step 4; 7.6 step 9).** Step 4 also refuses `reply_not_open` when the account's `auth.users.deleted_at` is set: the take-down marks it while it holds the profile FOR UPDATE, and the step runs after the profile's lock, so a reply that waited behind the take-down is refused; the profile is marked deleted only by the purge after it.
- **A reply's text when its decision holds nothing in force (6.5, 6.7, 7.14).** `erase_reply_statements` also erases an answered reply's text once the measure's decision holds nothing in force (`measures_in_force`), the moment an appeal of it is no longer open (`appeals_check`), not six months after the person was told.
- **The badge's undo (7.2's table, the row of setVerified).** The table says verifyBadge clears the phone hash it wrote when setVerified answers false. It writes back the hash it read before (`user.phoneHash`): an account that already had a badge keeps the number behind it, and that number is not freed for another account's badge.
- **'Nothing changed now' (3c's outcome line; 7.12).** The expression the status page and the outcome mail read (`answerChangedNothing`) also requires that no `retire_handle`, `suspend` or `terminate` of the answering decision changed something (`no_effect` null), so a reporter is never told that nothing changed beside 'korbat took a measure on the account'.
- **A decision about a measure on the terms names the terms (W.2, 10.6).** `DecisionStatement.reviewed` gains `basis` (the reviewed decision's suspension or termination's basis, null for none, absent before 3e), carried by the API's statement and the console's preview. A review, a correction, a lift or an answer to a reply whose reviewed measure rests on `strikes`, `ladder_end` or `protective` prints `STATEMENT_WORDS.ground.restedOnTerms` ('That decision rested on korbat's terms, section Suspension and termination.'), never 'That decision rested on korbat rule ...'.
- **The banner after an answered reply (9.1).** [banner.announced]'s last sentence, 'If you reply before it starts, it waits for korbat's answer.', is printed only while /me's `replyOpen` is true, for a suspension and a termination alike: after korbat answered the reply a second one is refused.
- **Cases (9.4).** `AuthorCaseRow` gains `standingMeasure` ({kind, days, announced}) and `liftedStanding` ({kind, replaced}). The rows read 'a suspension of {days} days, announced' or 'at once', 'a termination', 'suspension lifted', 'suspension withdrawn for another measure', 'termination lifted' (a word the design does not give: the lift of a termination read 'suspension lifted'), and on a reversal 'a suspension that rested on it ended' or 'a termination that rested on it ended' (the design names the first only). A kept correction, korbat's answer to a reply, reads 'korbat kept its decision' as a kept review does, never 'No action'. 'Your standing' prints the banner's sentences for a measure not fixed, announced, held or running, a termination included. A like, repost or bookmark on a card and a follow refused account_suspended show `RefusedNotice` (refusalSentence from /me with 'Read the decision'); `reporting_restricted` and `reply_not_open` are worded by the app's own sentences, never the server's.
- **Where it stands now (9.2).** The API sends a period's end cut to a lift or to the break of its basis, so `nowSentence` reads an end at that very moment as 'it was running then' ([now.lifted], [now.basis.running]) and only an earlier end as 'it had run out'.
- **[reports.marked] (9.4).** Its second sentence, 'You can ask for a re-examination.', is printed only while a re-examination of the item is open; otherwise the line is its first sentence alone (`STANDING_TEXTS.reports.markedClosed`).
- **The console's reply row of a termination (8.5).** A late reply to a termination reads 'after the start: the termination runs' and names no end.
- **Lab C (12.3).** C1's wave behind a holder that only locks the row is asserted (no write commits at or after the start), and two further waves run on accounts of their own, behind a holder that changes the other party's rows and behind a decision that holds the post FOR UPDATE; each of the three waves sends every route of 7.3 that a suspension refuses (post, reply, quote, like, repost, bookmark, follow, the profile's edit, the handle, an upload, the badge, a report under a rule). The integration file `standing-closing.test.ts` holds the same in 24 scenes, and the bound in a test of sixteen likers.
```

### Replace `packages/contracts/src/moderation.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";
import { Email, OpaqueId, TurnstileToken } from "./auth";
import { hex, sha256, sha256Bytes, sortedJson, utf8 } from "./canonical";
import { MediaId } from "./media";
import { FORBIDDEN_FORMAT } from "./text";

// Moderation cases (3c design, section 10): the constants and digests that the database, the API, the console, the app,
// the mails and the terms share. Each is the one source its words and numbers are taken from. This module imports
// nothing from staff.ts, and the index evaluates it first, so staff.ts can read these constants while it loads; an import
// the other way round would be a cycle that fails at load. For the same reason it imports nothing from social.ts, whose
// shapes may come to name this module's constants: what a notice needs of a post's id and of a handle is written here.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- rules, categories and keywords

/** The rulebook's rule ids. @korbat/rules holds the rules themselves; the contracts never import it. */
export const RULE_IDS = ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"] as const;
export type RuleId = (typeof RULE_IDS)[number];

/**
 * The 16 categories of the Commission's Transparency Database (read 2026-10-02), which every intake and decision carries.
 * The migration's CHECK lists are written from this constant, and a database test holds them to it. A value the
 * Commission removes stays here: a kept row may hold it, and only the lists offered for new input drop it.
 */
export const TDB_CATEGORIES = [
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS",
  "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
] as const;
export type TdbCategory = (typeof TDB_CATEGORIES)[number];

/** The two categories a notifier never chooses: a rule-only report gets the first, a notifier who is not sure the second. */
type UnofferedCategory = "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" | "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE";
export type TdbFormCategory = Exclude<TdbCategory, UnofferedCategory>;

/** The 14 categories the illegal-ground form shows. */
export const TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES: readonly TdbFormCategory[] = TDB_CATEGORIES.filter(
  (category): category is TdbFormCategory => category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC" && category !== "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE",
);

/**
 * The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material and the Transparency Database keyword each stores. "abuse"
 * stores none: the database has no keyword for it.
 */
export const CSAM_KEYWORDS = {
  csam: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL",
  deepfake: "KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE",
  grooming: "KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS",
  abuse: null,
} as const;
export type CsamKeywordChoice = keyof typeof CSAM_KEYWORDS;

/** The keywords a decision on the law may carry: in 3c only the Transparency Database's "Terrorist content". */
export const DECISION_KEYWORDS = ["KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT"] as const;
export type DecisionKeyword = (typeof DECISION_KEYWORDS)[number];

/** The category the composer presets for a decision under each rule. */
export const RULE_DEFAULT_CATEGORY = {
  R1: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
  R2: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS",
  R3: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH",
  R4: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS",
  R5: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE",
  R6: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD",
} as const satisfies Record<RuleId, TdbCategory>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- lanes

/** The queue's lanes: 0 is the most urgent. A case takes the most severe lane of its unanswered items. */
export type Lane = 0 | 1 | 2;

/** R2 and R5 are urgent; R3 and R4 come next; R1 and R6 last. */
const RULE_LANES: Record<RuleId, Lane> = { R1: 2, R2: 0, R3: 1, R4: 1, R5: 0, R6: 2 };

/** The categories that are not in lane 2: violence, public security and self-harm are urgent; six more come next. */
const CATEGORY_LANES: Partial<Record<TdbCategory, Lane>> = {
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM: 0,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS: 1,
  STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE: 1,
};

/**
 * The lane of an intake's items, from its ground alone: nothing is weighted. The CSAM path is urgent whatever else is
 * said. Otherwise it is the more severe of the cited rule's lane and, on a notice that alleges illegality, the category's:
 * only there is the category a claim about the content, where on a rule report or a finding it is korbat's own
 * classification for the Transparency Database.
 */
export function laneFor(input: { ruleId: RuleId | null; allegesIllegal: boolean; csam: boolean; category: TdbCategory }): Lane {
  if (input.csam) return 0;
  const byRule: Lane = input.ruleId === null ? 2 : RULE_LANES[input.ruleId];
  const byCategory: Lane = input.allegesIllegal ? (CATEGORY_LANES[input.category] ?? 2) : 2;
  return byRule < byCategory ? byRule : byCategory;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- limits and periods

/**
 * What one sender may send, published in the terms: intakes an hour and a day per network signed out and per account
 * signed in, the targets one notice names, and the bounds of its two texts in characters (the migration's CHECKs hold
 * the same numbers).
 */
export const NOTICE_LIMITS = {
  signedOut: { perHour: 5, perDay: 20 },
  signedIn: { perHour: 10, perDay: 50 },
  maxTargets: 10,
  explanationMax: 2000,
  citedLawMax: 300,
} as const;

/** A notice on the CSAM path names at most one account: one such target reaches every image on the account's posts. */
export const CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS = 1;

/** How many months back a case page counts earlier answers to reports of this kind about the same target or author. */
export const SUSPECT_EARLIER_MONTHS = 12;

/** How many rows of a seal's list the case answer carries. */
export const SEAL_LIST_MAX = 500;

/** The author's appeal and the re-examination window, in calendar months (appealDeadline, and appeal_deadline in SQL). */
export const APPEAL_MONTHS = 6;

/** Appeals a day per account, and re-examinations a day per account or network. */
export const DAILY_LIMITS = { appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 } as const;

/**
 * The numbers of account sanctions, the same as the SQL function standing_rules() returns, which a database test compares
 * member by member: every function and view of the standing ledger reads its numbers from there, and every word of the
 * console and the app from here. Each is a cautious default without a source of its own, flagged for the owner (3e
 * design, section 2): one line to change in each place. It stands here, ahead of the section of account sanctions below,
 * because RETENTION reads three of its numbers.
 */
export const STANDING_RULES = {
  /** How long a strike counts. */
  strikeDays: 90,
  /** The active strikes that open the ladder. */
  ladderStrikes: 3,
  /** The most days of the first, second and third suspension of the ladder. */
  ladderDays: [3, 7, 30],
  /** How long a suspension of the ladder counts toward the next rung. */
  ladderMemoryDays: 365,
  /** The reply window, from the moment korbat's own relay accepted the notice mail, and never less from the decision. */
  replyWindowHours: 168,
  /** The window, from the decision, when the relay refused the address or the mail was given up. */
  undeliveredHours: 336,
  /** The most days of a suspension at once, by its ground. */
  threatDays: 30,
  terroristDays: 30,
  floodDays: 7,
  protectiveDays: 14,

  floodPosts: 20,

  /** The most age of the decision a threat or terrorist suspension rests on, and of the seal for good a protective one rests on. */
  basisAgeDays: 30,

  reportFrameDays: 90,

  reportWarnMarks: 5,

  reportRestrictMarks: 3,

/**
 * How long 3c keeps each kind of data (the design's section 6.6), published in the terms. Each is a design choice, not a
 * legal figure.
 */
export const RETENTION = {
  /** Content restricted under R4 is erased once the restriction is final: this long after its author was told, or at the answer to their appeal. */
  r4FinalMonths: APPEAL_MONTHS,

  intakeDays: 30,

  evidenceHours: 24,

  accessLogMonths: 12,

  contactMaxMonths: 13,

  confirmationDays: 30,

   * old. No clock alone ends it, so it is a phrase, the one the terms print, and no number.

  standingRecord: { strikeDays: STANDING_RULES.strikeDays, ladderMemoryDays: STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays, warningDays: STANDING_RULES.reportFrameDays },

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- account sanctions (3e design, section 10.1)

/** What a standing measure or a restriction of reporting rests on, as the ledger's check trigger forces it. The migration's CHECK list is written from it. */

export type StandingBasis = (typeof STANDING_BASES)[number];

/** The bounds of `days` on a suspension and a restriction of reporting. */

/**

/** The most items one decision marks "manifestly unfounded" (a default, flagged with the other numbers). */

/**

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- measures

/**
 * The ledger's kinds, in the order of the database's action_kind: 3c's seven measures and five reversals, then 3e's six
 * measures (a strike, a suspension, a termination, a retired handle, a warning about reporting and a restriction of it)
 * and four reversals (3e design, section 10.1).
 */
export const ACTION_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "restore",
  "unseal_media",
  "restore_media",
  "restore_display_name",
  "restore_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
  "overrule",
  "lift_suspension",
  "unretire_handle",
  "lift_reporting",
] as const;
export type ActionKind = (typeof ACTION_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * What a measure acts on: a post, one image of it, every image its case reaches, one of an account's two fields, the
 * account itself (a strike, a suspension or a termination), its handle, or its reports under the rules.
 */
export type MeasureTarget = "post" | "image" | "images" | "display_name" | "bio" | "account" | "handle" | "reporting";

export interface MeasureSpec {
  /** A decision taken while deciding (interim) may hold it. */
  interim: boolean;
  /** A decision that decides the case (final) may hold it. */
  final: boolean;
  /** For a reversal, the measures it lifts (it names exactly one row of them); null for a measure. */
  lifts: readonly ActionKind[] | null;
  target: MeasureTarget;
  /** The words for it in the composer, the statement and the terms. */
  label: string;
}

/**
 * Every kind of the ledger: whether it is taken while deciding, when the case is decided, or is a reversal; its target;
 * and its label. A post or one image is withheld only while deciding and removed only when the case is decided; a seal
 * and a field reset are either. A reversal is neither: the database's triggers say which decision may hold one.
 */
export const MEASURES = {
  withhold: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Withhold the post" },
  remove: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "post", label: "Remove" },
  seal_media: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "images", label: "Seal the images this case reaches" },
  withhold_media: { interim: true, final: false, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Withhold one image" },
  remove_media: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "image", label: "Remove one image" },
  reset_display_name: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "display_name", label: "Reset display name" },
  reset_bio: { interim: true, final: true, lifts: null, target: "bio", label: "Reset bio" },
  restore: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold", "remove"], target: "post", label: "Lift the restriction of the post" },
  unseal_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["seal_media"], target: "images", label: "Lift the seal" },
  restore_media: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["withhold_media", "remove_media"], target: "image", label: "Lift the restriction of one image" },
  restore_display_name: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_display_name"], target: "display_name", label: "Lift the reset of the display name" },
  restore_bio: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["reset_bio"], target: "bio", label: "Lift the reset of the bio" },
  // 3e (design, section 18, W.1). Each measure of 3e is taken only when the case is decided, and none while deciding.
  strike: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Strike" },
  suspend: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Suspend the account" },
  terminate: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "account", label: "Terminate the account" },
  retire_handle: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "handle", label: "Retire the handle" },
  warn_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Warn about reporting" },
  restrict_reporting: { interim: false, final: true, lifts: null, target: "reporting", label: "Restrict reporting" },
  overrule: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["strike"], target: "account", label: "Overrule the strike" },
  lift_suspension: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["suspend", "terminate"], target: "account", label: "Lift the suspension" },
  unretire_handle: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["retire_handle"], target: "handle", label: "Give the handle back" },
  lift_reporting: { interim: false, final: false, lifts: ["warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting"], target: "reporting", label: "Lift the reporting measure" },
} as const satisfies Record<ActionKind, MeasureSpec>;

/** The thirteen measures and the nine reversals, each list in the ledger's order: what a statement's data keeps apart. */
export const MEASURE_KINDS = [
  "withhold",
  "remove",
  "seal_media",
  "withhold_media",
  "remove_media",
  "reset_display_name",
  "reset_bio",
  "strike",
  "suspend",
  "terminate",
  "retire_handle",
  "warn_reporting",
  "restrict_reporting",
] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type MeasureKind = (typeof MEASURE_KINDS)[number];
export const REVERSAL_KINDS = ["restore", "unseal_media", "restore_media", "restore_display_name", "restore_bio", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type ReversalKind = (typeof REVERSAL_KINDS)[number];

/** The three kinds whose action entry also signs `days` and `announced` (3e design, section 10.4). */
export const TIMED_KINDS = ["suspend", "terminate", "restrict_reporting"] as const satisfies readonly ActionKind[];
export type TimedKind = (typeof TIMED_KINDS)[number];

/**
 * The console's fixed drafts of the facts and the reason of a seal (3c design, section 10). Nobody at korbat opens images
 * that are reported as child sexual abuse material, so none of these says or implies that korbat found them to be such
 * material, and each reason says that korbat's staff do not open them: the statement then tells its author what korbat
 * knows and no more. The composer fills them in, and the moderator may edit them. The two `added` drafts are for a case
 * whose suspect items korbat added for a quoted post: they never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
 */
export const SEAL_DRAFTS = {
  facts: {
    notice_post: "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material.",
    notice_account: "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    notice_added: "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_post: "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material.",
    finding_account: "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
    finding_added: "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material.",
  },
  reason: {
    deciding: "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. It hides them from everyone, you included, until an admin has answered the report.",
    final:
      "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. An admin found the report credible enough to keep the images sealed and to report them to the police, who can assess them.",
  },
} as const;

/**
 * The facts draft of a seal, chosen from the suspect items its decision considers: a notice's draft when any of them came
 * from a user's notice, else a finding's; the `added` form when every one of them is an item korbat added for a quoted
 * post (or a re-examination of one), else the post's or the account's by the case's target.
 */
export function sealFactsDraft(target: "post" | "account", items: readonly { source: "user" | "finding"; added: boolean }[]): string {
  if (items.length === 0) throw new Error("a seal's facts are drafted from the suspect items its decision considers: there is no suspect item");
  const from = items.some((item) => item.source === "user") ? "notice" : "finding";
  const about = items.every((item) => item.added) ? "added" : target;
  return SEAL_DRAFTS.facts[`${from}_${about}`];
}

/**
 * One measure or reversal as a decision's confirmed params name it: its kind, and for an image measure the image; for a
 * suspension, a termination and a restriction of reporting also its days and whether it is announced (3e design,
 * section 10.4).
 */
export interface DecisionActionParams {
  kind: ActionKind;
  mediaId: string | null;
  days?: number | null;
  announced?: boolean;
}

/**
 * The one order a decision's actions are confirmed in: by kind and then by image, each compared as a string, an action
 * without an image first. The console sorts with it before it asks for the key, and the params' schema refuses any other
 * order, so the same decision always has the same hash.
 */
export function compareDecisionActions(a: DecisionActionParams, b: DecisionActionParams): number {
  if (a.kind !== b.kind) return a.kind < b.kind ? -1 : 1;
  const [left, right] = [a.mediaId ?? "", b.mediaId ?? ""];
  return left < right ? -1 : left > right ? 1 : 0;
}

/** Why a moderator reveals who sent a report: the choices of the reveal dialog. The reason itself is a saved text. */
export const REVEAL_REASON_CATEGORIES = ["impersonation_claim", "abuse_of_reporting", "legal_requirement", "other"] as const;
export type RevealReasonCategory = (typeof REVEAL_REASON_CATEGORIES)[number];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- errors

/**
 * Every code the moderation flows put in ErrorEnvelope.error.code: what sending a report or a notice, reading its
 * status, asking for a re-examination, appealing, taking a report in, deciding a case and reviewing an appeal raise, and
 * what the console's case routes answer (a text that cannot be saved, an image that is not shown, a source that cannot
 * be revealed). The routes may also answer the shared invalid_request, onboarding_required, not_found, rate_limited and
 * service_unavailable, and the staff routes the staff codes. The codes the database keeps to itself (moderation_column,
 * quote_item_missing, read_committed_only) are not among them: no route answers one.
 */
export const ModerationErrorCode = z.enum([
  "notice_link_invalid",
  "notice_link_offsite",
  "human_check_failed",
  "staff_cannot_report",
  "notice_not_found",
  "already_reported",
  "appeal_not_open",
  "appeal_exists",
  "reexamination_not_open",
  "reexamination_exists",
  "case_changed",
  "case_closed",
  "staff_recused",
  "staff_target",
  "admin_required",
  "reviewer_conflict",
  "decision_cap",
  "profile_changed",
  "snapshot_mismatch",
  "snapshot_erased",
  "text_not_found",
  "invalid_decision",
  "text_invalid",
  "text_quotes_user",
  "image_refused",
  "reveal_refused",
  // 3e (design, section 10.5): a rule report of an account whose reports are restricted, a reply to a measure that takes
  // none, a decision whose strike is missing or not due, a second standing measure, and a termination under R2.
  "reporting_restricted",
  "reply_not_open",
  "strike_mismatch",
  "standing_conflict",
  "ground_not_established",
]);
export type ModerationErrorCode = z.infer<typeof ModerationErrorCode>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- reports and notices

/**
 * The rules a report or a notice may cite. R2 is offered nowhere: a report of child sexual abuse material goes a path of
 * its own, which records no sender, and only a moderator's finding cites R2 (the database refuses a user's intake that
 * does).
 */
export const REPORT_RULE_IDS = ["R1", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"] as const satisfies readonly RuleId[];
export type ReportRuleId = (typeof REPORT_RULE_IDS)[number];

/** How many characters the name a signed-out notifier gives may have. */
export const NOTICE_NAME_MAX = 100;

/** Any control character but the line feed. */
const TEXT_CONTROL = /[^\P{Cc}\n]/u;
/** Any control character at all: a name is one line. */
const LINE_CONTROL = /\p{Cc}/u;

const NOT_WELL_FORMED = { message: "half of a surrogate pair is not text" };
const NO_CONTROL = { message: "control characters are not allowed" };
const NO_FORMAT = { message: "invisible direction and spacing characters are not allowed" };
const SOME_TEXT = { message: "some text is needed" };

/**
 * A free text of a notice. The server stores it as it was written or refuses it, and never changes it: a well-formed
 * string with some text in it, no control character but the line feed, none of the invisible direction and spacing
 * characters, and at most `max` characters as PostgreSQL's char_length counts them, which is what the tables' CHECKs hold.
 */
const noticeText = (max: number) =>
  z
    .string()
    // A character outside the basic plane is two UTF-16 units, so this bound never refuses what the count below accepts.
    .max(2 * max)
    .refine(isWellFormed, NOT_WELL_FORMED)
    .refine((text) => !TEXT_CONTROL.test(text), NO_CONTROL)
    .refine((text) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(text), NO_FORMAT)
    .refine((text) => text.trim().length > 0, SOME_TEXT)
    .refine((text) => Array.from(text).length <= max, { message: `at most ${max} characters` });

/** The name a signed-out notifier may give: one line under the same rules. */
const NotifierName = z
  .string()
  .max(2 * NOTICE_NAME_MAX)
  .refine(isWellFormed, NOT_WELL_FORMED)
  .refine((name) => !LINE_CONTROL.test(name), NO_CONTROL)
  .refine((name) => !FORBIDDEN_FORMAT.test(name), NO_FORMAT)
  .refine((name) => name.trim().length > 0, SOME_TEXT)
  .refine((name) => Array.from(name).length <= NOTICE_NAME_MAX, { message: `at most ${NOTICE_NAME_MAX} characters` });

/** A post's id in the lower case PostgreSQL returns, so an id written in any case names the same row. */
const TargetPostId = z.uuid().transform((id) => id.toLowerCase());

/** A handle as a notice names it: an optional leading @, then the 3 to 20 characters handles may contain, kept in lower case. */
const TargetHandle = z
  .string()
  .trim()
  .regex(/^@?[A-Za-z0-9_]{3,20}$/)
  .transform((value) => value.replace(/^@/, "").toLowerCase());

/**
 * A link as a notice gives it: an http or https address of at most 300 characters, kept as written. Whether it is an
 * address of this korbat, and of what, the route decides.
 */
const TargetLink = z.url({ protocol: /^https?$/ }).max(300);

/**
 * What a report or a notice names: a post by its id, optionally with the one of its images that is meant; an account by
 * its handle; or a korbat link, which the server parses. Nothing else can be named, and nothing can be attached.
 */
export const NoticeTarget = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("post"), id: TargetPostId, mediaId: MediaId.optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("account"), handle: TargetHandle }),
  z.strictObject({ kind: z.literal("link"), url: TargetLink }),
]);
export type NoticeTarget = z.infer<typeof NoticeTarget>;

const NoticeTargets = z.array(NoticeTarget).min(1).max(NOTICE_LIMITS.maxTargets);
const ReportRule = z.enum(REPORT_RULE_IDS);

/** The categories an illegal-ground notice may carry: the 14 the form shows, and "not specified" for someone who is not sure. */
const NoticeCategory = z.enum([...TDB_FORM_CATEGORIES, "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE"] as const);

/** The four choices of the path for child sexual abuse material. */
const CsamChoice = z.enum(Object.keys(CSAM_KEYWORDS) as [CsamKeywordChoice, ...CsamKeywordChoice[]]);

/**
 * One report or notice, by its ground. Each ground is a strict shape, so a member that belongs to another ground is
 * refused rather than ignored:
 *   - `rule`: it breaks a korbat rule (any but R2), with an optional explanation;
 *   - `illegal`: an Art. 16 notice that it is illegal, with the category, the explanation and the statement of good
 *     faith the Article asks for, optionally the law, a rule it also breaks and, from someone signed out, a name and an
 *     address (a signed-in sender's contact is their account, and the route refuses either from them);
 *   - `csam`: the path for child sexual abuse material, which asks no name or address and records no sender; its
 *     explanation and statement are optional, and it names at most CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS accounts, counted by the
 *     handles as named (the route counts again once the links are parsed).
 * `turnstileToken` is the human check of a signed-out sender; a signed-in sender's is ignored.
 */
export const NoticeRequest = z.discriminatedUnion("ground", [
  z.strictObject({
    ground: z.literal("rule"),
    ruleId: ReportRule,
    targets: NoticeTargets,
    explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax).optional(),
    turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
  }),
  z.strictObject({
    ground: z.literal("illegal"),
    targets: NoticeTargets,
    category: NoticeCategory,
    citedLaw: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.citedLawMax).optional(),
    explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax),
    bonaFide: z.literal(true),
    ruleId: ReportRule.optional(),
    name: NotifierName.optional(),
    email: Email.optional(),
    turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
  }),
  z
    .strictObject({
      ground: z.literal("csam"),
      targets: NoticeTargets,
      keyword: CsamChoice,
      explanation: noticeText(NOTICE_LIMITS.explanationMax).optional(),
      bonaFide: z.boolean().optional(),
      turnstileToken: TurnstileToken.optional(),
    })
    .refine((notice) => new Set(notice.targets.flatMap((target) => (target.kind === "account" ? [target.handle] : []))).size <= CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS, {
      message: `a notice of this kind names at most ${CSAM_NOTICE_MAX_ACCOUNTS} account`,
      path: ["targets"],
    }),
]);
export type NoticeRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeRequest>;

/** A notice's public reference: N- and ten base32 characters. */
export const NoticeRef = z.string().regex(/^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$/);

/**
 * The answer to a report or a notice. The token comes only with a notice sent signed out or on the path for child sexual
 * abuse material: it opens the status page, and is shown once.
 */
export const NoticeResponse = z.object({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId.optional() });
export type NoticeResponse = z.infer<typeof NoticeResponse>;

/** What the status page sends: the reference with the notice's own token, or with the token of a mail's link. */
export const NoticeStatusRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId });
export type NoticeStatusRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeStatusRequest>;

/** The page's two buttons, for which only the token of a mail's link works: "I sent this", or "stop korbat's mails about reports to this address". */
export const NoticeContactRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId, choice: z.enum(["confirm", "stop"]) });
export type NoticeContactRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeContactRequest>;

/**
 * The longest statement an appeal or a request for a re-examination may carry, in characters as PostgreSQL's
 * char_length counts them: what the CHECKs of `appeals` and `intake_items` hold.
 */
export const STATEMENT_MAX = 2000;

/**
 * What the person may add to an appeal or to a request for a re-examination: free of form and optional, under the
 * rules of every free text of a notice. Left out when they wrote nothing.
 */
const Statement = noticeText(STATEMENT_MAX).optional();

/**
 * POST /api/notices/reexamine: a notifier asks korbat to decide an item of their notice again, with the notice's own
 * token or the token of a mail's link, as for the status page. `position` is the item's place on that page, 1 to 20:
 * an item korbat added for a quoted post is asked about like any other, by its own position.
 */
export const NoticeReexamineRequest = z.strictObject({ ref: NoticeRef, token: OpaqueId, position: z.number().int().min(1).max(20), statement: Statement });
export type NoticeReexamineRequest = z.infer<typeof NoticeReexamineRequest>;

/** POST /api/moderation/items/:item/reexamine: the same, for an item of a report the signed-in account sent, named by its id. */
export const ReexamineRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: Statement });
export type ReexamineRequest = z.infer<typeof ReexamineRequest>;

/** POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/appeal: the author's appeal of a final decision that restricts them. */
export const AppealRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: Statement });
export type AppealRequest = z.infer<typeof AppealRequest>;

/**
 * POST /api/moderation/decisions/:id/reply (3e design, sections 7.6 step 9 and 10.2): the person's one reply to the
 * suspension or termination a decision holds, with an optional text under the text rules, at most REPLY_TEXT_MAX
 * characters. The server makes its salt and digest, as for an appeal.
 */
export const ReplyRequest = z.strictObject({ statement: noticeText(REPLY_TEXT_MAX).optional() });
export type ReplyRequest = z.infer<typeof ReplyRequest>;

/** The answer to a reply (201): when the database filed it, and whether it came before the start, which it then holds. */
export const ReplyResponse = z.object({ filedAt: z.iso.datetime(), onTime: z.boolean() });
export type ReplyResponse = z.infer<typeof ReplyResponse>;

/**
 * The answer to a request for a re-examination (201): the positions of the items that are now examined again, in
 * order. One, or two when the item is a report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another and the
 * item korbat added for the quoted post could be examined again too: korbat then examines both.
 */
export const ReexamineResponse = z.object({ positions: z.array(z.number().int().min(1).max(20)).min(1).max(2) });
export type ReexamineResponse = z.infer<typeof ReexamineResponse>;

/** What an item's sender can be shown, as the database's item_outcome lists them. */
export const ITEM_OUTCOMES = ["restricted_rule", "restricted_legal", "no_violation", "not_evident", "not_available", "partly_reversed", "reversed"] as const;
export const ItemOutcome = z.enum(ITEM_OUTCOMES);
export type ItemOutcome = z.infer<typeof ItemOutcome>;

/**
 * One phrase for each outcome, which the mails, the status page and the app's list all take from here (3c design,
 * section 10). `{rule}` and `{title}` stand for the rule the restricting decision cites, in the wording of the rulebook
 * it was made under. A reader composes a whole answer with outcomeWords, never from these alone.
 */
export const OUTCOME_PHRASES = {
  restricted_rule: "access restricted: it breaks korbat rule {rule} ({title})",
  restricted_legal: "access restricted: korbat found it illegal",
  no_violation: "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal",
  not_evident: "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules, and whether it is illegal cannot be seen without a detailed legal examination; a court or an authority can order its removal",
  not_available: "no action: the link names nothing korbat can show (checked automatically)",
  partly_reversed: "korbat reversed part of its decision to restrict it",
  reversed: "korbat reversed its decision to restrict it",
} as const satisfies Record<ItemOutcome, string>;

/** After a restricting outcome whose decision's measures all changed nothing when they were imposed. */
export const ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN = "It was already not shown on korbat, so nothing changed now; korbat's restriction stays in force should that change.";

/** After the outcome of an item about an account that is not suspect and whose answering decision sealed nothing. */
export const ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE = "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio. korbat decides about its posts and images in cases of their own and does not report those here.";

/**
 * 3e (design, section 10.1 and W.1): in place of ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE, after the outcome of an item about an account whose
 * answering decision holds an account measure of 3e. `retired` whenever that decision retires the handle, which anyone can
 * see on the profile; `measure` otherwise (the suspensions and the termination taken at once, which Task 3 opens). Neither
 * names a suspension, an access or a duration, so that nothing a reporter reads lets them follow the account's standing.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE = {
  retired: "korbat retired the handle.",
  measure: "korbat took a measure on the account. It does not report here which, or for how long.",
} as const;

/** After the outcome of an item about a post that quotes another (never a suspect item, whose quoted post has an item of its own). */
export const QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE = "This answer concerns this post's own text and images. korbat decides about the post it quotes, shown inside its card, in a case of its own and does not report that here.";

/** After the outcome of an item about an account that is suspect, or that a decision holding a seal answered: that answer does concern the images on the account's posts. */
export const ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE =
  "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio and, taken together, the images on its posts. korbat decides about single posts of the account, and about what its posts say, in cases of their own and does not report those here.";

/**
 * On the path for child sexual abuse material nobody opens the images, so no item is shown words that say korbat found
 * something about them. `sealed` stands for every item whose answering decision holds a seal, suspect or not, in place of
 * the two restricting phrases; `no_action` for a suspect item answered without action, in place of the two no-action ones.
 */
export const SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES = {
  sealed: "access restricted: korbat sealed its images without opening them. They are shown to nobody, their author included, and are kept for the authorities.",
  no_action:
    "no action: korbat's staff do not open images reported this way. An admin found in the report, and in what korbat can read and still holds of it, no sufficient ground to seal images or to restrict anything else.",
} as const;

/** After the restricting phrase of a suspect item that a decision answered by a measure on the post's text, without a seal. */
export const SUSPECT_NO_SEAL = "No image was sealed; korbat's staff do not open images reported this way.";

/**
 * For an item on another ground about a post that a decision answered without action while nobody could open the post's
 * images (decisions.unseen), in place of the two no-action phrases: it tells its sender the truth, and such an answer
 * does not spend the one re-examination.
 */
export const UNSEEN_NO_ACTION =
  "no action for now: when korbat decided, its staff could not open this post's images, because a report of another kind about them was waiting or they were sealed. If your report is about an image, ask for a re-examination.";

/** What decides how one item's outcome reads: the facts of the item and of the decision that answered it. */
export interface OutcomeWordsInput {
  outcome: ItemOutcome;
  /** The rule a `restricted_rule` outcome names, with its title in the rulebook the decision was made under; null for every other outcome. */
  rule: { id: string; title: string } | null;
  /** The item itself is suspect: a report of child sexual abuse material, or a finding citing R2. */
  suspect: boolean;
  /** The answering decision holds a seal. */
  sealed: boolean;
  /** The answering decision was taken while nobody could open the post's images, and the item is about a post and not suspect. */
  unseen: boolean;
  /** Every measure of the answering decision changed nothing when it was imposed. */
  noEffect: boolean;
  /** What the answer concerns, as the status answer gives it. */
  scope: "account" | "quote" | "account_suspect" | "account_retired" | "account_measure" | null;
}

const NO_ACTION: readonly ItemOutcome[] = ["no_violation", "not_evident"];
const RESTRICTING: readonly ItemOutcome[] = ["restricted_rule", "restricted_legal"];

/** A phrase as a sentence: with the one full stop it ends in. */
const sentence = (phrase: string): string => (phrase.endsWith(".") ? phrase : `${phrase}.`);

/**
 * One item's outcome as its sender reads it, in a mail's line, on the status page and in the app's list alike: the
 * outcome's phrase, then the sentences that follow it, in this order (3c design, section 7.8, step 4, and section 10).
 *   - The phrase. A restriction by a decision that holds a seal reads the `sealed` phrase, whatever the item's ground. A
 *     suspect item answered without action reads the `no_action` phrase. An item on another ground about a post, answered
 *     without action with the images out of sight, reads UNSEEN_NO_ACTION; an item about an account never does, since its
 *     answer concerns the display name and bio, which staff read. Every other outcome reads its own phrase, also a
 *     reversal and a link that named nothing on that path.
 *   - SUSPECT_NO_SEAL, after a suspect item's restriction that sealed nothing.
 *   - ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN, after a restricting outcome whose measures all changed nothing.
 *   - The scope's sentence, after every outcome but `not_available`; 3e's retired phrase only after a restricting one, since
 *     a reversal's phrase says on its own that the handle was given back, and a sentence that it was retired would contradict it.
 * The text ends in one full stop.
 */
export function outcomeWords(input: OutcomeWordsInput): string {
  const { outcome, scope } = input;
  const aboutAccount = scope === "account" || scope === "account_suspect";
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (RESTRICTING.includes(outcome) && input.sealed) {
    parts.push(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
  } else if (NO_ACTION.includes(outcome) && input.suspect) {
    parts.push(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
  } else if (NO_ACTION.includes(outcome) && input.unseen && !aboutAccount) {
    parts.push(UNSEEN_NO_ACTION);
  } else if (outcome === "restricted_rule") {
    if (input.rule === null) throw new Error("a restriction under a rule is worded with its rule: none was given");
    const { id, title } = input.rule;
    // Each placeholder is filled by a function, so that no character of an id or a title is read as a pattern.
    parts.push(sentence(OUTCOME_PHRASES.restricted_rule.replace("{rule}", () => id).replace("{title}", () => title)));
  } else {
    parts.push(sentence(OUTCOME_PHRASES[outcome]));
  }
  if (RESTRICTING.includes(outcome)) {
    if (input.suspect && !input.sealed) parts.push(SUSPECT_NO_SEAL);
    if (input.noEffect) parts.push(ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN);
  }
  if (outcome !== "not_available") {
    if (scope === "account") parts.push(ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE);
    if (scope === "account_suspect") parts.push(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE);
    if (scope === "quote") parts.push(QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE);
    if (scope === "account_retired" && RESTRICTING.includes(outcome)) parts.push(ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.retired);
    // 3e (7.11 item 7): a suspension or termination taken at once that answered the item, named by no word of what it is.
    if (scope === "account_measure" && RESTRICTING.includes(outcome)) parts.push(ACCOUNT_MEASURE_SCOPE.measure);
  }
  return parts.join(" ");
}

/**
 * One item of a notice as its sender reads it. `link` is the item's korbat address, an account's built from the handle
 * as the notice named it and never from the handle the profile holds now. `scope` says what the answer concerns
 * (`account`, `quote`, `account_suspect`, `account_retired`, `account_measure`, or null). An item about an account carries its scope from
 * the first moment, whatever the handle named: `account_suspect` when the item is suspect or, once released, when its
 * answering decision sealed images; once released, `account_retired` (3e) when that decision retired the handle,
 * `account_measure` (3e) when it took a suspension or termination at once and retired no handle; and
 * `account` otherwise. `quote`, for a post that quotes another, comes only with the released outcome, so that before
```
